Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Shanbah, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn Yaḥyawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Umayyah Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I used to pass by this verse not knowing what al-ʿashiyy and al-ishrāq were, until Umm Hānīʾ bint Abī Ṭālib told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer, and said: 'O Umm Hānīʾ, this is the prayer of ishrāq.'" [110] [Musnad al-Ḥumaydī: 1/160; Musnad Ibn Rāhawayh: 5/19.]

ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There remained in my mind something about the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) until I sought it in the Qur'an and found it in this verse: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq."

ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿAbbās did not used to pray the forenoon prayer, and then he prayed it afterwards.

It is related that Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said to Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I find in the Book of Allah a prayer after the rising of the sun."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I will show you that in the Book of Allah, in the story of Dāwūd: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq; and al-ishrāq is not the rising of the sun, rather it is its clarity and brightness."

Wa al-ṭayra, that is, and We subjected the birds to him, maḥshūrah, gathered; kullun lahu, that is, to Dāwūd, awwāb, obedient. Wa shadadnā mulkahu, that is, We strengthened his kingdom.

Al-Ḥasan recited: wa shaddadnā with the doubling of the dāl.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was the mightiest of the kings of the earth in authority; every night thirty-three thousand men would guard his sanctuary (miḥrāb). That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom," through the guard.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man from the Children of Israel sought redress against a man of their notables, and the two came before the Prophet Dāwūd. The complainant said: "This man has seized my cow from me."

Dāwūd asked the man about it, and he denied it; he asked the other for proof, and he had no proof. Dāwūd said to them both: "Wait until I consider your affair."

They rose from his presence, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dāwūd (peace be upon him) in a dream that he should kill the man against whom redress was sought.

He said: "This is a dream, and I will not hasten until I am certain."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him a second time that he should kill him, but he did not do so. Allah revealed to him a third time: that he should kill him, or the punishment from Allah would come to him. Dāwūd sent for the man and said: "Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you."

The man said: "You would kill me without proof or certainty!" Dāwūd said: "Yes, by Allah, I will surely carry out the command of Allah concerning you."

When the man knew that he was about to kill him, he said: "Do not hasten until I tell you: by Allah, I was not seized for this sin, but I had secretly killed this man's father, and for that I have been seized."

Dāwūd then ordered him put to death, and his awe grew among the Children of Israel at that time for Dāwūd, and his kingdom became firm through it. That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom."

Wa ātaynāhu al-ḥikmah, that is, prophethood and correctness in affairs. Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: knowledge that the intellects do not reject.

Wa faṣla al-khiṭāb. Ibn ʿAbbās said: clarity of speech.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Kalbī, Ibn Masʿūd, Muqātil and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: it means the knowledge of judgment and insight into adjudication, such that he would not stammer in judging between people; and this is one of the reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: it is the proof upon the claimant and the oath upon the one who denies.

Akhbarnā Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Jawrī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Bakr Bālawayh ibn Muḥammad ibn Bālawayh al-Mirbatānī there, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Ḥawnī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Khamīṣamī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Aḥmad, who said: Akhbarnā Sharīk from al-Aʿmash from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Kaʿb regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths."

Anbaʾanī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid, who said: Akhbarnā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Ḥaddathanā Wahb ibn Jarīr, who said: Akhbarnā [Shuʿbah] from al-Ḥakam from Shurayḥ regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths." This is also the view of Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sumrah al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abī Shaybah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf al-Azraq from Zakariyyā, that is Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from [al-Subayʿī], who said: I heard Ziyād say: "Faṣla al-khiṭāb, which was given to Dāwūd, is 'amma baʿd,' and he was the first to say it."

Wa hal atāka naba' al-khaṣm (al-āyah). The scholars differed, in the reports of the prophets, concerning the reason Allah tested His Prophet Dāwūd with the sin with which he was tested.

Some people said: the cause of that was that one day he wished of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, the station of his forefathers Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb (peace be upon them), and asked that He test him in the manner in which He had tested them, and give him the bounty similar to what He had given them.

Al-Suddī, al-Kalbī and Muqātil related from their shaykhs, the narrations of some entering into others, they said: Dāwūd had divided time into three days: a day in which he judged between the people, a day in which he withdrew for the worship of his Lord, and a day in which he withdrew for his wives and his affairs. He found in what he read of the books the excellence of Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, and said:

"O Lord, all the good has been taken by my forefathers who came before me."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "They were tested with trials, with which you were not tested, and they were patient with them. Ibrāhīm was tested with Nimrod and with the slaughter of his son; Isḥāq was tested with being slaughtered and with the loss of his sight; Yaʿqūb was tested with grief over Yūsuf. And you have not been tested with any of that."

Dāwūd said: "My Lord, then test me with the like of what You tested them with, and give me the like of what You gave them."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "You will be tested in such-and-such a month, on such-and-such a day, so be on guard."

When that day which Allah had promised came, Dāwūd entered his sanctuary, closed its door, and began to pray and recite the Zabūr. While he was thus, Satan came to him in the form of a dove of gold with every beautiful color, and it fell between his feet. He stretched out his hand to take it and give it to a young son of his, but when he reached for it, it flew off not far away, without despairing him of itself; he extended his hand to take it, and it moved away, and he followed it, until it flew and landed in a window; he went to take it, and it flew out of the window. Dāwūd looked to see where it would fall, and he sent someone to catch it, and they saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. This is the saying of al-Kalbī.

Al-Suddī said: He saw her bathing on her roof, and he saw a woman of the most beautiful form, and Dāwūd marveled at her beauty. She turned, and saw his shadow, and she shook out her hair, which covered her body, and this increased his admiration for her, so he asked about her. It was said: she is Tashāyiʿ, daughter of Shāyiʿ, the wife of Uriyā ibn Ḥanānā, and her husband was on a campaign in al-Balqāʾ with Ayyūb ibn Ṣūriyā, the son of Dāwūd's sister.

Dāwūd wrote to his nephew Ayyūb, commander in al-Balqāʾ: "Send Uriyā to such-and-such a place, and put him forward before the Ark; and whoever is put forward before the Ark may not return behind it until Allah grants victory at his hands or he is martyred." So he sent him forward, and victory was granted at his hands, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, which is fiercer than that." He sent him, and victory was granted, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, fiercer in might than that." He sent him, and he was killed the third time. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dāwūd married her, and she is the mother of Sulaymān. [This story is a fable from which Allah keeps His friends, let alone His prophets; it appears in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/175; Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī: 1/338; and Mustadrak al-Ḥākim: 2/586.]

Others said: the cause of his trial was that his soul told him he could endure a day without committing any fault.

This is what Shuʿayb ibn Muḥammad informed us, who said: Akhbarnā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar, who said: Ḥaddathanā Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd from Maṭar from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd divided time into four parts: a day for his wives, a day for worship, a day for judging among the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, to remind them and be reminded by them, to make them weep and weep with them.

He said: When the day of the Children of Israel came, they mentioned and said: "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?"

Dāwūd resolved in himself that he would achieve that. When the day of his worship came, he locked his doors and ordered that no one enter upon him, and he devoted himself to reading the Torah. While he was reading, a golden dove with every beautiful color fell between his hands; he reached out to take it, but it flew and landed not far off, without despairing him of itself; he kept following it until he came upon a woman bathing; her form and beauty pleased him, and when she saw his shadow on the ground, she covered herself with her hair, which increased his admiration for her. He had sent her husband upon one of his armies, and he wrote to him: "Go to such-and-such a place," a place such that whoever went there would be killed and not return. He did so, and he was struck down. Dāwūd then proposed to her, and married her. [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/176; Tafsīr al-Ṣanʿānī: 3/161.]

Some said concerning the cause of that: Akhbarnā Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar al-Bāqirjī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlawiyyah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ismāʿīl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd ibn Bashīr from Qatādah from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd said to the Children of Israel when he became king: "By Allah, I will surely be just among you." He did not make the exception (by saying "in shāʾ Allāh"), so he was tested with it. [Zād al-Masīr: 6/326.]

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Warrāq said: The cause of that was that Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was much devoted to worship, and he was pleased with his knowledge, and said: "Is there anyone on earth who does my deeds?"

Then Jibrīl came to him and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: You have been pleased with your worship, and self-admiration devours worship. If you are pleased a second time, I will leave you to yourself."

He said: "My Lord, leave me to myself for a year."
He said: "Indeed it is a great deal."
He said: "Then an hour."
He said: "Then do as you will with it."

So he appointed guards, put on wool, entered the prayer niche (mihrab), and placed the Psalms (al-Zabur) before him. While he was in his devotion and worship, the bird suddenly landed before him, and what happened with the woman happened.

They said: When Dawud married the wife of Uriah, she had not stayed long before God, glory be to Him, sent two angels in the form of men. They asked to enter upon him, but they found him on his day of worship, and the guards prevented them from entering upon him. So they scaled the niche (mihrab) over him, and he did not notice until, while he was praying, they were sitting before him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/175.] This is His saying:

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche?﴾

They used a plural verb because "khasm" (adversary, litigant) is a noun that applies to the singular, the dual, and the plural, and to the masculine and the feminine alike.

Labid said:

*And adversaries who rush to enter, as if they were proud stallions, each bright-faced and well-bred...* [Lisan al-Arab: 12/180.]

Another poet said:

*And fierce adversaries who shake their beards, like the shaking of thoroughbred, well-bred horses...* [Fath al-Qadir: 4/425.]

The plural was used for the two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, so two and whatever is above them is a group, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].

Bal lammā (rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment; had they tasted it, they would not have said this). Am ʿindahum khazāʾinu raḥmati rabbika al-ʿazīzi al-wahhāb? (Or do they possess the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?) That is, the keys of prophethood; its parallel is in Surat al-Zukhruf: "Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?" [Q. 43:32], meaning the prophethood of your Lord. Am lahum mulku al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi wa mā baynahumā, falyartaqū fī al-asbāb? (Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend by the means.) That is, let them climb the mountains up to the heavens, and bring down revelation from there to whomever they choose and wish. This is a rebuke and a challenge to their incapacity.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mujāhid and Qatādah said: by "al-asbāb" is meant the gates of heaven and its paths.

Jundun mā hunālika mahzūmun min al-aḥzāb: they are an army there, defeated, prevented from ascending to the heavens, among the confederates (al-aḥzāb, the factions).

Most exegetes said: the meaning is that these chieftains who make this statement are a defeated, subdued army, while you (O Muhammad) are victorious and triumphant over them.

Qatādah said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised him in Makkah that He would defeat them, and its fulfilment came on the Day of Badr, [defeat of] the confederates, as with the earlier generations who were subdued and destroyed. Then He said, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ): Kadhdhabat qablahum qawmu Nūḥin wa ʿĀdun wa Firʿawnu dhū al-awtād. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "dhū al-awtād" means one of firm construction.

Al-Qutaybī said: The Arabs say, "They are in firmly-rooted might, and a firmly-rooted kingdom," meaning it is enduring and strong, and the origin of this is that a tent of theirs stands by its pegs (awtād).

Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said: "In the shade of a kingdom whose pegs are firm."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "dhū al-awtād" means possessor of strength and force.

Al-Ḥalabī and Muqātil said: He used to punish people with pegs. When he was angry with someone, he would stretch him out on his back between four pegs, each of his feet to a pillar and each of his hands to a pillar, and leave him thus suspended in the air between heaven and earth until he died.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: He would stretch the man out lying on the ground, then fasten him with pegs.

Al-Suddī said: He would stretch the man and fasten him with pegs, and send upon him scorpions and snakes.

Qatādah and ʿAṭāʾ said: He had pegs and cords (arsāl) and playthings (malāʿib) upon which he would amuse himself before his eyes.

Wa Thamūdu wa qawmu Lūṭin wa aṣḥābu al-Aykah, ulāʾika al-aḥzāb. In kullun illā kadhdhaba al-rusula fa-ḥaqqa ʿiqāb: each of them only denied the messengers, so My punishment became due and befell them.

Wa mā yanẓuru hāʾulāʾi, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan, which is the blast of the Resurrection.

This interpretation has been related traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mā lahā min fawāq.

Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: "from return." Al-Wālibī: "increase." Mujāhid: "a respite." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "rest."

There are two readings: fuwāq with a ḍamma on the fāʾ, the dialect of Tamīm, and the reading of Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf; and fawāq with a fatḥa, the dialect of Quraysh, the reading of the rest of the readers, and the choice of Abū ʿUbayd.

Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says ḥamām al-mukkūk and ḥamāmuhu, and qiṣāṣ al-shaʿr and qiṣāṣuhu. Others distinguished between them.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mu'arrikh said: with a fatḥa it means rest and recovery, like jawāb from ijābah, taking it to mean the patient's recovery from his illness; and al-fawāq with a ḍamma is the interval between two milkings, that is, one milks the she-camel, then leaves her for a while until the milk gathers; the interval between the two milkings is a fuwāq. It was then borrowed for the sense of waiting for a short period.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands guard for the interval of a she-camel's milking in the way of Allah, Allah forbids his body to the Fire." [Al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr of al-Suyūṭī: 2/603, no. 8692; Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 4/307, no. 10634.] [108]

Wa qālū rabbanā ʿajjil lanā qiṭṭanā qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: "that is, our book."

Also from him: "al-qiṭṭ is the scroll that has counted everything."

Abu al-ʿĀliyah and al-Kalbī said: when there was revealed in al-Ḥāqqah, "As for him who is given his book in his right hand" [Q. 69:19] and "As for him who is given his book in his left hand" [Q. 69:25].

They said, in mockery: "Hasten for us our qiṭṭ," meaning our book, hasten it for us in this world, qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: it means our punishment and what has been decreed for us of torment.

ʿAṭāʾ said: this was said by al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and it is his saying: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."

And he is the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall" [Q. 70:1]. ʿAṭāʾ said: some dozen verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning him.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they mean their share and portion of the Garden which is spoken of.

Al-Farrāʾ said: al-qiṭṭ in the speech of the Arabs means a share, and from it the written document (al-ṣakk) is called qiṭṭ.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: al-qiṭṭ is a book of gifts (bi-al-jawāʾah).

al-Aʿshā said:
"Nor the king al-Nuʿmān on the day I met him, giving with bounty the qiṭūṭ, and generous."

He means books of rewards, that is, with virtue and eminence. It is said a horse is afiq and a she-camel afiqah when they are noble and preferred over others.

Mujāhid said: qiṭṭanā means our reckoning, and the book of reckoning is called qiṭṭ; the root of the word is from writing.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Iṣbir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna, wa dhkur ʿabdanā Dāwūda dhā al-ayd: possessor of strength in worship. Innahu awwāb: obedient.

From Ibn ʿAbbās: returning repeatedly to repentance.

From al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: he is the one who glorifies (al-musabbiḥ) in the Ethiopian tongue.

Akhbarnī al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Dīnawarī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Faḍl ibn al-Faḍl al-Kindī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn [Fāris] in Baghdad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAmr ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from al-Zuhrī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Blueness is a sign of Yemen, and Dāwūd the Prophet (peace be upon him) was blue-eyed." [See: al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr: 2/33; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 6/17.] [109]

Innā sakhkharnā al-jibāla maʿahu yusabbiḥna: with his glorification.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: he used to understand the glorification of stone and tree.

Bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Shanbah, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn Yaḥyawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Umayyah Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I used to pass by this verse not knowing what al-ʿashiyy and al-ishrāq were, until Umm Hānīʾ bint Abī Ṭālib told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer, and said: 'O Umm Hānīʾ, this is the prayer of ishrāq.'" [110] [Musnad al-Ḥumaydī: 1/160; Musnad Ibn Rāhawayh: 5/19.]

ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There remained in my mind something about the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) until I sought it in the Qur'an and found it in this verse: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq."

ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿAbbās did not used to pray the forenoon prayer, and then he prayed it afterwards.

It is related that Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said to Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I find in the Book of Allah a prayer after the rising of the sun."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I will show you that in the Book of Allah, in the story of Dāwūd: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq; and al-ishrāq is not the rising of the sun, rather it is its clarity and brightness."

Wa al-ṭayra, that is, and We subjected the birds to him, maḥshūrah, gathered; kullun lahu, that is, to Dāwūd, awwāb, obedient. Wa shadadnā mulkahu, that is, We strengthened his kingdom.

Al-Ḥasan recited: wa shaddadnā with the doubling of the dāl.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was the mightiest of the kings of the earth in authority; every night thirty-three thousand men would guard his sanctuary (miḥrāb). That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom," through the guard.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man from the Children of Israel sought redress against a man of their notables, and the two came before the Prophet Dāwūd. The complainant said: "This man has seized my cow from me."

Dāwūd asked the man about it, and he denied it; he asked the other for proof, and he had no proof. Dāwūd said to them both: "Wait until I consider your affair."

They rose from his presence, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dāwūd (peace be upon him) in a dream that he should kill the man against whom redress was sought.

He said: "This is a dream, and I will not hasten until I am certain."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him a second time that he should kill him, but he did not do so. Allah revealed to him a third time: that he should kill him, or the punishment from Allah would come to him. Dāwūd sent for the man and said: "Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you."

The man said: "You would kill me without proof or certainty!" Dāwūd said: "Yes, by Allah, I will surely carry out the command of Allah concerning you."

When the man knew that he was about to kill him, he said: "Do not hasten until I tell you: by Allah, I was not seized for this sin, but I had secretly killed this man's father, and for that I have been seized."

Dāwūd then ordered him put to death, and his awe grew among the Children of Israel at that time for Dāwūd, and his kingdom became firm through it. That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom."

Wa ātaynāhu al-ḥikmah, that is, prophethood and correctness in affairs. Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: knowledge that the intellects do not reject.

Wa faṣla al-khiṭāb. Ibn ʿAbbās said: clarity of speech.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Kalbī, Ibn Masʿūd, Muqātil and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: it means the knowledge of judgment and insight into adjudication, such that he would not stammer in judging between people; and this is one of the reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: it is the proof upon the claimant and the oath upon the one who denies.

Akhbarnā Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Jawrī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Bakr Bālawayh ibn Muḥammad ibn Bālawayh al-Mirbatānī there, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Ḥawnī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Khamīṣamī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Aḥmad, who said: Akhbarnā Sharīk from al-Aʿmash from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Kaʿb regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths."

Anbaʾanī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid, who said: Akhbarnā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Ḥaddathanā Wahb ibn Jarīr, who said: Akhbarnā [Shuʿbah] from al-Ḥakam from Shurayḥ regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths." This is also the view of Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sumrah al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abī Shaybah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf al-Azraq from Zakariyyā, that is Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from [al-Subayʿī], who said: I heard Ziyād say: "Faṣla al-khiṭāb, which was given to Dāwūd, is 'amma baʿd,' and he was the first to say it."

Wa hal atāka naba' al-khaṣm (al-āyah). The scholars differed, in the reports of the prophets, concerning the reason Allah tested His Prophet Dāwūd with the sin with which he was tested.

Some people said: the cause of that was that one day he wished of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, the station of his forefathers Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb (peace be upon them), and asked that He test him in the manner in which He had tested them, and give him the bounty similar to what He had given them.

Al-Suddī, al-Kalbī and Muqātil related from their shaykhs, the narrations of some entering into others, they said: Dāwūd had divided time into three days: a day in which he judged between the people, a day in which he withdrew for the worship of his Lord, and a day in which he withdrew for his wives and his affairs. He found in what he read of the books the excellence of Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, and said:

"O Lord, all the good has been taken by my forefathers who came before me."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "They were tested with trials, with which you were not tested, and they were patient with them. Ibrāhīm was tested with Nimrod and with the slaughter of his son; Isḥāq was tested with being slaughtered and with the loss of his sight; Yaʿqūb was tested with grief over Yūsuf. And you have not been tested with any of that."

Dāwūd said: "My Lord, then test me with the like of what You tested them with, and give me the like of what You gave them."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "You will be tested in such-and-such a month, on such-and-such a day, so be on guard."

When that day which Allah had promised came, Dāwūd entered his sanctuary, closed its door, and began to pray and recite the Zabūr. While he was thus, Satan came to him in the form of a dove of gold with every beautiful color, and it fell between his feet. He stretched out his hand to take it and give it to a young son of his, but when he reached for it, it flew off not far away, without despairing him of itself; he extended his hand to take it, and it moved away, and he followed it, until it flew and landed in a window; he went to take it, and it flew out of the window. Dāwūd looked to see where it would fall, and he sent someone to catch it, and they saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. This is the saying of al-Kalbī.

Al-Suddī said: He saw her bathing on her roof, and he saw a woman of the most beautiful form, and Dāwūd marveled at her beauty. She turned, and saw his shadow, and she shook out her hair, which covered her body, and this increased his admiration for her, so he asked about her. It was said: she is Tashāyiʿ, daughter of Shāyiʿ, the wife of Uriyā ibn Ḥanānā, and her husband was on a campaign in al-Balqāʾ with Ayyūb ibn Ṣūriyā, the son of Dāwūd's sister.

Dāwūd wrote to his nephew Ayyūb, commander in al-Balqāʾ: "Send Uriyā to such-and-such a place, and put him forward before the Ark; and whoever is put forward before the Ark may not return behind it until Allah grants victory at his hands or he is martyred." So he sent him forward, and victory was granted at his hands, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, which is fiercer than that." He sent him, and victory was granted, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, fiercer in might than that." He sent him, and he was killed the third time. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dāwūd married her, and she is the mother of Sulaymān. [This story is a fable from which Allah keeps His friends, let alone His prophets; it appears in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/175; Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī: 1/338; and Mustadrak al-Ḥākim: 2/586.]

Others said: the cause of his trial was that his soul told him he could endure a day without committing any fault.

This is what Shuʿayb ibn Muḥammad informed us, who said: Akhbarnā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar, who said: Ḥaddathanā Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd from Maṭar from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd divided time into four parts: a day for his wives, a day for worship, a day for judging among the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, to remind them and be reminded by them, to make them weep and weep with them.

He said: When the day of the Children of Israel came, they mentioned and said: "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?"

Dāwūd resolved in himself that he would achieve that. When the day of his worship came, he locked his doors and ordered that no one enter upon him, and he devoted himself to reading the Torah. While he was reading, a golden dove with every beautiful color fell between his hands; he reached out to take it, but it flew and landed not far off, without despairing him of itself; he kept following it until he came upon a woman bathing; her form and beauty pleased him, and when she saw his shadow on the ground, she covered herself with her hair, which increased his admiration for her. He had sent her husband upon one of his armies, and he wrote to him: "Go to such-and-such a place," a place such that whoever went there would be killed and not return. He did so, and he was struck down. Dāwūd then proposed to her, and married her. [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/176; Tafsīr al-Ṣanʿānī: 3/161.]

Some said concerning the cause of that: Akhbarnā Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar al-Bāqirjī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlawiyyah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ismāʿīl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd ibn Bashīr from Qatādah from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd said to the Children of Israel when he became king: "By Allah, I will surely be just among you." He did not make the exception (by saying "in shāʾ Allāh"), so he was tested with it. [Zād al-Masīr: 6/326.]

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Warrāq said: The cause of that was that Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was much devoted to worship, and he was pleased with his knowledge, and said: "Is there anyone on earth who does my deeds?"

Then Jibrīl came to him and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: You have been pleased with your worship, and self-admiration devours worship. If you are pleased a second time, I will leave you to yourself."

He said: "My Lord, leave me to myself for a year."
He said: "Indeed it is a great deal."
He said: "Then an hour."
He said: "Then do as you will with it."

So he appointed guards, put on wool, entered the prayer niche (mihrab), and placed the Psalms (al-Zabur) before him. While he was in his devotion and worship, the bird suddenly landed before him, and what happened with the woman happened.

They said: When Dawud married the wife of Uriah, she had not stayed long before God, glory be to Him, sent two angels in the form of men. They asked to enter upon him, but they found him on his day of worship, and the guards prevented them from entering upon him. So they scaled the niche (mihrab) over him, and he did not notice until, while he was praying, they were sitting before him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/175.] This is His saying:

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche?﴾

They used a plural verb because "khasm" (adversary, litigant) is a noun that applies to the singular, the dual, and the plural, and to the masculine and the feminine alike.

Labid said:

*And adversaries who rush to enter, as if they were proud stallions, each bright-faced and well-bred...* [Lisan al-Arab: 12/180.]

Another poet said:

*And fierce adversaries who shake their beards, like the shaking of thoroughbred, well-bred horses...* [Fath al-Qadir: 4/425.]

The plural was used for the two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, so two and whatever is above them is a group, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].

Bal lammā (rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment; had they tasted it, they would not have said this). Am ʿindahum khazāʾinu raḥmati rabbika al-ʿazīzi al-wahhāb? (Or do they possess the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?) That is, the keys of prophethood; its parallel is in Surat al-Zukhruf: "Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?" [Q. 43:32], meaning the prophethood of your Lord. Am lahum mulku al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi wa mā baynahumā, falyartaqū fī al-asbāb? (Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend by the means.) That is, let them climb the mountains up to the heavens, and bring down revelation from there to whomever they choose and wish. This is a rebuke and a challenge to their incapacity.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mujāhid and Qatādah said: by "al-asbāb" is meant the gates of heaven and its paths.

Jundun mā hunālika mahzūmun min al-aḥzāb: they are an army there, defeated, prevented from ascending to the heavens, among the confederates (al-aḥzāb, the factions).

Most exegetes said: the meaning is that these chieftains who make this statement are a defeated, subdued army, while you (O Muhammad) are victorious and triumphant over them.

Qatādah said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised him in Makkah that He would defeat them, and its fulfilment came on the Day of Badr, [defeat of] the confederates, as with the earlier generations who were subdued and destroyed. Then He said, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ): Kadhdhabat qablahum qawmu Nūḥin wa ʿĀdun wa Firʿawnu dhū al-awtād. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "dhū al-awtād" means one of firm construction.

Al-Qutaybī said: The Arabs say, "They are in firmly-rooted might, and a firmly-rooted kingdom," meaning it is enduring and strong, and the origin of this is that a tent of theirs stands by its pegs (awtād).

Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said: "In the shade of a kingdom whose pegs are firm."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "dhū al-awtād" means possessor of strength and force.

Al-Ḥalabī and Muqātil said: He used to punish people with pegs. When he was angry with someone, he would stretch him out on his back between four pegs, each of his feet to a pillar and each of his hands to a pillar, and leave him thus suspended in the air between heaven and earth until he died.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: He would stretch the man out lying on the ground, then fasten him with pegs.

Al-Suddī said: He would stretch the man and fasten him with pegs, and send upon him scorpions and snakes.

Qatādah and ʿAṭāʾ said: He had pegs and cords (arsāl) and playthings (malāʿib) upon which he would amuse himself before his eyes.

Wa Thamūdu wa qawmu Lūṭin wa aṣḥābu al-Aykah, ulāʾika al-aḥzāb. In kullun illā kadhdhaba al-rusula fa-ḥaqqa ʿiqāb: each of them only denied the messengers, so My punishment became due and befell them.

Wa mā yanẓuru hāʾulāʾi, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan, which is the blast of the Resurrection.

This interpretation has been related traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mā lahā min fawāq.

Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: "from return." Al-Wālibī: "increase." Mujāhid: "a respite." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "rest."

There are two readings: fuwāq with a ḍamma on the fāʾ, the dialect of Tamīm, and the reading of Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf; and fawāq with a fatḥa, the dialect of Quraysh, the reading of the rest of the readers, and the choice of Abū ʿUbayd.

Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says ḥamām al-mukkūk and ḥamāmuhu, and qiṣāṣ al-shaʿr and qiṣāṣuhu. Others distinguished between them.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mu'arrikh said: with a fatḥa it means rest and recovery, like jawāb from ijābah, taking it to mean the patient's recovery from his illness; and al-fawāq with a ḍamma is the interval between two milkings, that is, one milks the she-camel, then leaves her for a while until the milk gathers; the interval between the two milkings is a fuwāq. It was then borrowed for the sense of waiting for a short period.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands guard for the interval of a she-camel's milking in the way of Allah, Allah forbids his body to the Fire." [Al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr of al-Suyūṭī: 2/603, no. 8692; Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 4/307, no. 10634.] [108]

Wa qālū rabbanā ʿajjil lanā qiṭṭanā qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: "that is, our book."

Also from him: "al-qiṭṭ is the scroll that has counted everything."

Abu al-ʿĀliyah and al-Kalbī said: when there was revealed in al-Ḥāqqah, "As for him who is given his book in his right hand" [Q. 69:19] and "As for him who is given his book in his left hand" [Q. 69:25].

They said, in mockery: "Hasten for us our qiṭṭ," meaning our book, hasten it for us in this world, qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: it means our punishment and what has been decreed for us of torment.

ʿAṭāʾ said: this was said by al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and it is his saying: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."

And he is the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall" [Q. 70:1]. ʿAṭāʾ said: some dozen verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning him.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they mean their share and portion of the Garden which is spoken of.

Al-Farrāʾ said: al-qiṭṭ in the speech of the Arabs means a share, and from it the written document (al-ṣakk) is called qiṭṭ.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: al-qiṭṭ is a book of gifts (bi-al-jawāʾah).

al-Aʿshā said:
"Nor the king al-Nuʿmān on the day I met him, giving with bounty the qiṭūṭ, and generous."

He means books of rewards, that is, with virtue and eminence. It is said a horse is afiq and a she-camel afiqah when they are noble and preferred over others.

Mujāhid said: qiṭṭanā means our reckoning, and the book of reckoning is called qiṭṭ; the root of the word is from writing.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Iṣbir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna, wa dhkur ʿabdanā Dāwūda dhā al-ayd: possessor of strength in worship. Innahu awwāb: obedient.

From Ibn ʿAbbās: returning repeatedly to repentance.

From al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: he is the one who glorifies (al-musabbiḥ) in the Ethiopian tongue.

Akhbarnī al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Dīnawarī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Faḍl ibn al-Faḍl al-Kindī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn [Fāris] in Baghdad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAmr ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from al-Zuhrī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Blueness is a sign of Yemen, and Dāwūd the Prophet (peace be upon him) was blue-eyed." [See: al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr: 2/33; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 6/17.] [109]

Innā sakhkharnā al-jibāla maʿahu yusabbiḥna: with his glorification.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: he used to understand the glorification of stone and tree.

Bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Shanbah, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn Yaḥyawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Umayyah Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I used to pass by this verse not knowing what al-ʿashiyy and al-ishrāq were, until Umm Hānīʾ bint Abī Ṭālib told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer, and said: 'O Umm Hānīʾ, this is the prayer of ishrāq.'" [110] [Musnad al-Ḥumaydī: 1/160; Musnad Ibn Rāhawayh: 5/19.]

ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There remained in my mind something about the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) until I sought it in the Qur'an and found it in this verse: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq."

ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿAbbās did not used to pray the forenoon prayer, and then he prayed it afterwards.

It is related that Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said to Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I find in the Book of Allah a prayer after the rising of the sun."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I will show you that in the Book of Allah, in the story of Dāwūd: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq; and al-ishrāq is not the rising of the sun, rather it is its clarity and brightness."

Wa al-ṭayra, that is, and We subjected the birds to him, maḥshūrah, gathered; kullun lahu, that is, to Dāwūd, awwāb, obedient. Wa shadadnā mulkahu, that is, We strengthened his kingdom.

Al-Ḥasan recited: wa shaddadnā with the doubling of the dāl.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was the mightiest of the kings of the earth in authority; every night thirty-three thousand men would guard his sanctuary (miḥrāb). That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom," through the guard.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man from the Children of Israel sought redress against a man of their notables, and the two came before the Prophet Dāwūd. The complainant said: "This man has seized my cow from me."

Dāwūd asked the man about it, and he denied it; he asked the other for proof, and he had no proof. Dāwūd said to them both: "Wait until I consider your affair."

They rose from his presence, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dāwūd (peace be upon him) in a dream that he should kill the man against whom redress was sought.

He said: "This is a dream, and I will not hasten until I am certain."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him a second time that he should kill him, but he did not do so. Allah revealed to him a third time: that he should kill him, or the punishment from Allah would come to him. Dāwūd sent for the man and said: "Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you."

The man said: "You would kill me without proof or certainty!" Dāwūd said: "Yes, by Allah, I will surely carry out the command of Allah concerning you."

When the man knew that he was about to kill him, he said: "Do not hasten until I tell you: by Allah, I was not seized for this sin, but I had secretly killed this man's father, and for that I have been seized."

Dāwūd then ordered him put to death, and his awe grew among the Children of Israel at that time for Dāwūd, and his kingdom became firm through it. That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom."

Wa ātaynāhu al-ḥikmah, that is, prophethood and correctness in affairs. Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: knowledge that the intellects do not reject.

Wa faṣla al-khiṭāb. Ibn ʿAbbās said: clarity of speech.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Kalbī, Ibn Masʿūd, Muqātil and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: it means the knowledge of judgment and insight into adjudication, such that he would not stammer in judging between people; and this is one of the reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: it is the proof upon the claimant and the oath upon the one who denies.

Akhbarnā Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Jawrī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Bakr Bālawayh ibn Muḥammad ibn Bālawayh al-Mirbatānī there, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Ḥawnī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Khamīṣamī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Aḥmad, who said: Akhbarnā Sharīk from al-Aʿmash from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Kaʿb regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths."

Anbaʾanī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid, who said: Akhbarnā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Ḥaddathanā Wahb ibn Jarīr, who said: Akhbarnā [Shuʿbah] from al-Ḥakam from Shurayḥ regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths." This is also the view of Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sumrah al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abī Shaybah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf al-Azraq from Zakariyyā, that is Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from [al-Subayʿī], who said: I heard Ziyād say: "Faṣla al-khiṭāb, which was given to Dāwūd, is 'amma baʿd,' and he was the first to say it."

Wa hal atāka naba' al-khaṣm (al-āyah). The scholars differed, in the reports of the prophets, concerning the reason Allah tested His Prophet Dāwūd with the sin with which he was tested.

Some people said: the cause of that was that one day he wished of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, the station of his forefathers Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb (peace be upon them), and asked that He test him in the manner in which He had tested them, and give him the bounty similar to what He had given them.

Al-Suddī, al-Kalbī and Muqātil related from their shaykhs, the narrations of some entering into others, they said: Dāwūd had divided time into three days: a day in which he judged between the people, a day in which he withdrew for the worship of his Lord, and a day in which he withdrew for his wives and his affairs. He found in what he read of the books the excellence of Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, and said:

"O Lord, all the good has been taken by my forefathers who came before me."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "They were tested with trials, with which you were not tested, and they were patient with them. Ibrāhīm was tested with Nimrod and with the slaughter of his son; Isḥāq was tested with being slaughtered and with the loss of his sight; Yaʿqūb was tested with grief over Yūsuf. And you have not been tested with any of that."

Dāwūd said: "My Lord, then test me with the like of what You tested them with, and give me the like of what You gave them."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "You will be tested in such-and-such a month, on such-and-such a day, so be on guard."

When that day which Allah had promised came, Dāwūd entered his sanctuary, closed its door, and began to pray and recite the Zabūr. While he was thus, Satan came to him in the form of a dove of gold with every beautiful color, and it fell between his feet. He stretched out his hand to take it and give it to a young son of his, but when he reached for it, it flew off not far away, without despairing him of itself; he extended his hand to take it, and it moved away, and he followed it, until it flew and landed in a window; he went to take it, and it flew out of the window. Dāwūd looked to see where it would fall, and he sent someone to catch it, and they saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. This is the saying of al-Kalbī.

Al-Suddī said: He saw her bathing on her roof, and he saw a woman of the most beautiful form, and Dāwūd marveled at her beauty. She turned, and saw his shadow, and she shook out her hair, which covered her body, and this increased his admiration for her, so he asked about her. It was said: she is Tashāyiʿ, daughter of Shāyiʿ, the wife of Uriyā ibn Ḥanānā, and her husband was on a campaign in al-Balqāʾ with Ayyūb ibn Ṣūriyā, the son of Dāwūd's sister.

Dāwūd wrote to his nephew Ayyūb, commander in al-Balqāʾ: "Send Uriyā to such-and-such a place, and put him forward before the Ark; and whoever is put forward before the Ark may not return behind it until Allah grants victory at his hands or he is martyred." So he sent him forward, and victory was granted at his hands, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, which is fiercer than that." He sent him, and victory was granted, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, fiercer in might than that." He sent him, and he was killed the third time. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dāwūd married her, and she is the mother of Sulaymān. [This story is a fable from which Allah keeps His friends, let alone His prophets; it appears in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/175; Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī: 1/338; and Mustadrak al-Ḥākim: 2/586.]

Others said: the cause of his trial was that his soul told him he could endure a day without committing any fault.

This is what Shuʿayb ibn Muḥammad informed us, who said: Akhbarnā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar, who said: Ḥaddathanā Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd from Maṭar from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd divided time into four parts: a day for his wives, a day for worship, a day for judging among the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, to remind them and be reminded by them, to make them weep and weep with them.

He said: When the day of the Children of Israel came, they mentioned and said: "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?"

Dāwūd resolved in himself that he would achieve that. When the day of his worship came, he locked his doors and ordered that no one enter upon him, and he devoted himself to reading the Torah. While he was reading, a golden dove with every beautiful color fell between his hands; he reached out to take it, but it flew and landed not far off, without despairing him of itself; he kept following it until he came upon a woman bathing; her form and beauty pleased him, and when she saw his shadow on the ground, she covered herself with her hair, which increased his admiration for her. He had sent her husband upon one of his armies, and he wrote to him: "Go to such-and-such a place," a place such that whoever went there would be killed and not return. He did so, and he was struck down. Dāwūd then proposed to her, and married her. [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/176; Tafsīr al-Ṣanʿānī: 3/161.]

Some said concerning the cause of that: Akhbarnā Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar al-Bāqirjī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlawiyyah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ismāʿīl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd ibn Bashīr from Qatādah from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd said to the Children of Israel when he became king: "By Allah, I will surely be just among you." He did not make the exception (by saying "in shāʾ Allāh"), so he was tested with it. [Zād al-Masīr: 6/326.]

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Warrāq said: The cause of that was that Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was much devoted to worship, and he was pleased with his knowledge, and said: "Is there anyone on earth who does my deeds?"

Then Jibrīl came to him and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: You have been pleased with your worship, and self-admiration devours worship. If you are pleased a second time, I will leave you to yourself."

He said: "My Lord, leave me to myself for a year."
He said: "Indeed it is a great deal."
He said: "Then an hour."
He said: "Then do as you will with it."

So he appointed guards, put on wool, entered the prayer niche (mihrab), and placed the Psalms (al-Zabur) before him. While he was in his devotion and worship, the bird suddenly landed before him, and what happened with the woman happened.

They said: When Dawud married the wife of Uriah, she had not stayed long before God, glory be to Him, sent two angels in the form of men. They asked to enter upon him, but they found him on his day of worship, and the guards prevented them from entering upon him. So they scaled the niche (mihrab) over him, and he did not notice until, while he was praying, they were sitting before him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/175.] This is His saying:

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche?﴾

They used a plural verb because "khasm" (adversary, litigant) is a noun that applies to the singular, the dual, and the plural, and to the masculine and the feminine alike.

Labid said:

*And adversaries who rush to enter, as if they were proud stallions, each bright-faced and well-bred...* [Lisan al-Arab: 12/180.]

Another poet said:

*And fierce adversaries who shake their beards, like the shaking of thoroughbred, well-bred horses...* [Fath al-Qadir: 4/425.]

The plural was used for the two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, so two and whatever is above them is a group, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].

Bal lammā (rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment; had they tasted it, they would not have said this). Am ʿindahum khazāʾinu raḥmati rabbika al-ʿazīzi al-wahhāb? (Or do they possess the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?) That is, the keys of prophethood; its parallel is in Surat al-Zukhruf: "Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?" [Q. 43:32], meaning the prophethood of your Lord. Am lahum mulku al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi wa mā baynahumā, falyartaqū fī al-asbāb? (Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend by the means.) That is, let them climb the mountains up to the heavens, and bring down revelation from there to whomever they choose and wish. This is a rebuke and a challenge to their incapacity.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mujāhid and Qatādah said: by "al-asbāb" is meant the gates of heaven and its paths.

Jundun mā hunālika mahzūmun min al-aḥzāb: they are an army there, defeated, prevented from ascending to the heavens, among the confederates (al-aḥzāb, the factions).

Most exegetes said: the meaning is that these chieftains who make this statement are a defeated, subdued army, while you (O Muhammad) are victorious and triumphant over them.

Qatādah said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised him in Makkah that He would defeat them, and its fulfilment came on the Day of Badr, [defeat of] the confederates, as with the earlier generations who were subdued and destroyed. Then He said, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ): Kadhdhabat qablahum qawmu Nūḥin wa ʿĀdun wa Firʿawnu dhū al-awtād. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "dhū al-awtād" means one of firm construction.

Al-Qutaybī said: The Arabs say, "They are in firmly-rooted might, and a firmly-rooted kingdom," meaning it is enduring and strong, and the origin of this is that a tent of theirs stands by its pegs (awtād).

Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said: "In the shade of a kingdom whose pegs are firm."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "dhū al-awtād" means possessor of strength and force.

Al-Ḥalabī and Muqātil said: He used to punish people with pegs. When he was angry with someone, he would stretch him out on his back between four pegs, each of his feet to a pillar and each of his hands to a pillar, and leave him thus suspended in the air between heaven and earth until he died.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: He would stretch the man out lying on the ground, then fasten him with pegs.

Al-Suddī said: He would stretch the man and fasten him with pegs, and send upon him scorpions and snakes.

Qatādah and ʿAṭāʾ said: He had pegs and cords (arsāl) and playthings (malāʿib) upon which he would amuse himself before his eyes.

Wa Thamūdu wa qawmu Lūṭin wa aṣḥābu al-Aykah, ulāʾika al-aḥzāb. In kullun illā kadhdhaba al-rusula fa-ḥaqqa ʿiqāb: each of them only denied the messengers, so My punishment became due and befell them.

Wa mā yanẓuru hāʾulāʾi, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan, which is the blast of the Resurrection.

This interpretation has been related traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mā lahā min fawāq.

Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: "from return." Al-Wālibī: "increase." Mujāhid: "a respite." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "rest."

There are two readings: fuwāq with a ḍamma on the fāʾ, the dialect of Tamīm, and the reading of Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf; and fawāq with a fatḥa, the dialect of Quraysh, the reading of the rest of the readers, and the choice of Abū ʿUbayd.

Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says ḥamām al-mukkūk and ḥamāmuhu, and qiṣāṣ al-shaʿr and qiṣāṣuhu. Others distinguished between them.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mu'arrikh said: with a fatḥa it means rest and recovery, like jawāb from ijābah, taking it to mean the patient's recovery from his illness; and al-fawāq with a ḍamma is the interval between two milkings, that is, one milks the she-camel, then leaves her for a while until the milk gathers; the interval between the two milkings is a fuwāq. It was then borrowed for the sense of waiting for a short period.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands guard for the interval of a she-camel's milking in the way of Allah, Allah forbids his body to the Fire." [Al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr of al-Suyūṭī: 2/603, no. 8692; Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 4/307, no. 10634.] [108]

Wa qālū rabbanā ʿajjil lanā qiṭṭanā qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: "that is, our book."

Also from him: "al-qiṭṭ is the scroll that has counted everything."

Abu al-ʿĀliyah and al-Kalbī said: when there was revealed in al-Ḥāqqah, "As for him who is given his book in his right hand" [Q. 69:19] and "As for him who is given his book in his left hand" [Q. 69:25].

They said, in mockery: "Hasten for us our qiṭṭ," meaning our book, hasten it for us in this world, qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: it means our punishment and what has been decreed for us of torment.

ʿAṭāʾ said: this was said by al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and it is his saying: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."

And he is the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall" [Q. 70:1]. ʿAṭāʾ said: some dozen verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning him.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they mean their share and portion of the Garden which is spoken of.

Al-Farrāʾ said: al-qiṭṭ in the speech of the Arabs means a share, and from it the written document (al-ṣakk) is called qiṭṭ.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: al-qiṭṭ is a book of gifts (bi-al-jawāʾah).

al-Aʿshā said:
"Nor the king al-Nuʿmān on the day I met him, giving with bounty the qiṭūṭ, and generous."

He means books of rewards, that is, with virtue and eminence. It is said a horse is afiq and a she-camel afiqah when they are noble and preferred over others.

Mujāhid said: qiṭṭanā means our reckoning, and the book of reckoning is called qiṭṭ; the root of the word is from writing.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Iṣbir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna, wa dhkur ʿabdanā Dāwūda dhā al-ayd: possessor of strength in worship. Innahu awwāb: obedient.

From Ibn ʿAbbās: returning repeatedly to repentance.

From al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: he is the one who glorifies (al-musabbiḥ) in the Ethiopian tongue.

Akhbarnī al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Dīnawarī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Faḍl ibn al-Faḍl al-Kindī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn [Fāris] in Baghdad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAmr ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from al-Zuhrī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Blueness is a sign of Yemen, and Dāwūd the Prophet (peace be upon him) was blue-eyed." [See: al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr: 2/33; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 6/17.] [109]

Innā sakhkharnā al-jibāla maʿahu yusabbiḥna: with his glorification.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: he used to understand the glorification of stone and tree.

Bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Shanbah, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn Yaḥyawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Umayyah Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I used to pass by this verse not knowing what al-ʿashiyy and al-ishrāq were, until Umm Hānīʾ bint Abī Ṭālib told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer, and said: 'O Umm Hānīʾ, this is the prayer of ishrāq.'" [110] [Musnad al-Ḥumaydī: 1/160; Musnad Ibn Rāhawayh: 5/19.]

ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There remained in my mind something about the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) until I sought it in the Qur'an and found it in this verse: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq."

ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿAbbās did not used to pray the forenoon prayer, and then he prayed it afterwards.

It is related that Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said to Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I find in the Book of Allah a prayer after the rising of the sun."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I will show you that in the Book of Allah, in the story of Dāwūd: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq; and al-ishrāq is not the rising of the sun, rather it is its clarity and brightness."

Wa al-ṭayra, that is, and We subjected the birds to him, maḥshūrah, gathered; kullun lahu, that is, to Dāwūd, awwāb, obedient. Wa shadadnā mulkahu, that is, We strengthened his kingdom.

Al-Ḥasan recited: wa shaddadnā with the doubling of the dāl.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was the mightiest of the kings of the earth in authority; every night thirty-three thousand men would guard his sanctuary (miḥrāb). That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom," through the guard.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man from the Children of Israel sought redress against a man of their notables, and the two came before the Prophet Dāwūd. The complainant said: "This man has seized my cow from me."

Dāwūd asked the man about it, and he denied it; he asked the other for proof, and he had no proof. Dāwūd said to them both: "Wait until I consider your affair."

They rose from his presence, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dāwūd (peace be upon him) in a dream that he should kill the man against whom redress was sought.

He said: "This is a dream, and I will not hasten until I am certain."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him a second time that he should kill him, but he did not do so. Allah revealed to him a third time: that he should kill him, or the punishment from Allah would come to him. Dāwūd sent for the man and said: "Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you."

The man said: "You would kill me without proof or certainty!" Dāwūd said: "Yes, by Allah, I will surely carry out the command of Allah concerning you."

When the man knew that he was about to kill him, he said: "Do not hasten until I tell you: by Allah, I was not seized for this sin, but I had secretly killed this man's father, and for that I have been seized."

Dāwūd then ordered him put to death, and his awe grew among the Children of Israel at that time for Dāwūd, and his kingdom became firm through it. That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom."

Wa ātaynāhu al-ḥikmah, that is, prophethood and correctness in affairs. Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: knowledge that the intellects do not reject.

Wa faṣla al-khiṭāb. Ibn ʿAbbās said: clarity of speech.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Kalbī, Ibn Masʿūd, Muqātil and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: it means the knowledge of judgment and insight into adjudication, such that he would not stammer in judging between people; and this is one of the reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: it is the proof upon the claimant and the oath upon the one who denies.

Akhbarnā Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Jawrī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Bakr Bālawayh ibn Muḥammad ibn Bālawayh al-Mirbatānī there, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Ḥawnī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Khamīṣamī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Aḥmad, who said: Akhbarnā Sharīk from al-Aʿmash from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Kaʿb regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths."

Anbaʾanī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid, who said: Akhbarnā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Ḥaddathanā Wahb ibn Jarīr, who said: Akhbarnā [Shuʿbah] from al-Ḥakam from Shurayḥ regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths." This is also the view of Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sumrah al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abī Shaybah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf al-Azraq from Zakariyyā, that is Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from [al-Subayʿī], who said: I heard Ziyād say: "Faṣla al-khiṭāb, which was given to Dāwūd, is 'amma baʿd,' and he was the first to say it."

Wa hal atāka naba' al-khaṣm (al-āyah). The scholars differed, in the reports of the prophets, concerning the reason Allah tested His Prophet Dāwūd with the sin with which he was tested.

Some people said: the cause of that was that one day he wished of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, the station of his forefathers Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb (peace be upon them), and asked that He test him in the manner in which He had tested them, and give him the bounty similar to what He had given them.

Al-Suddī, al-Kalbī and Muqātil related from their shaykhs, the narrations of some entering into others, they said: Dāwūd had divided time into three days: a day in which he judged between the people, a day in which he withdrew for the worship of his Lord, and a day in which he withdrew for his wives and his affairs. He found in what he read of the books the excellence of Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, and said:

"O Lord, all the good has been taken by my forefathers who came before me."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "They were tested with trials, with which you were not tested, and they were patient with them. Ibrāhīm was tested with Nimrod and with the slaughter of his son; Isḥāq was tested with being slaughtered and with the loss of his sight; Yaʿqūb was tested with grief over Yūsuf. And you have not been tested with any of that."

Dāwūd said: "My Lord, then test me with the like of what You tested them with, and give me the like of what You gave them."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "You will be tested in such-and-such a month, on such-and-such a day, so be on guard."

When that day which Allah had promised came, Dāwūd entered his sanctuary, closed its door, and began to pray and recite the Zabūr. While he was thus, Satan came to him in the form of a dove of gold with every beautiful color, and it fell between his feet. He stretched out his hand to take it and give it to a young son of his, but when he reached for it, it flew off not far away, without despairing him of itself; he extended his hand to take it, and it moved away, and he followed it, until it flew and landed in a window; he went to take it, and it flew out of the window. Dāwūd looked to see where it would fall, and he sent someone to catch it, and they saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. This is the saying of al-Kalbī.

Al-Suddī said: He saw her bathing on her roof, and he saw a woman of the most beautiful form, and Dāwūd marveled at her beauty. She turned, and saw his shadow, and she shook out her hair, which covered her body, and this increased his admiration for her, so he asked about her. It was said: she is Tashāyiʿ, daughter of Shāyiʿ, the wife of Uriyā ibn Ḥanānā, and her husband was on a campaign in al-Balqāʾ with Ayyūb ibn Ṣūriyā, the son of Dāwūd's sister.

Dāwūd wrote to his nephew Ayyūb, commander in al-Balqāʾ: "Send Uriyā to such-and-such a place, and put him forward before the Ark; and whoever is put forward before the Ark may not return behind it until Allah grants victory at his hands or he is martyred." So he sent him forward, and victory was granted at his hands, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, which is fiercer than that." He sent him, and victory was granted, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, fiercer in might than that." He sent him, and he was killed the third time. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dāwūd married her, and she is the mother of Sulaymān. [This story is a fable from which Allah keeps His friends, let alone His prophets; it appears in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/175; Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī: 1/338; and Mustadrak al-Ḥākim: 2/586.]

Others said: the cause of his trial was that his soul told him he could endure a day without committing any fault.

This is what Shuʿayb ibn Muḥammad informed us, who said: Akhbarnā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar, who said: Ḥaddathanā Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd from Maṭar from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd divided time into four parts: a day for his wives, a day for worship, a day for judging among the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, to remind them and be reminded by them, to make them weep and weep with them.

He said: When the day of the Children of Israel came, they mentioned and said: "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?"

Dāwūd resolved in himself that he would achieve that. When the day of his worship came, he locked his doors and ordered that no one enter upon him, and he devoted himself to reading the Torah. While he was reading, a golden dove with every beautiful color fell between his hands; he reached out to take it, but it flew and landed not far off, without despairing him of itself; he kept following it until he came upon a woman bathing; her form and beauty pleased him, and when she saw his shadow on the ground, she covered herself with her hair, which increased his admiration for her. He had sent her husband upon one of his armies, and he wrote to him: "Go to such-and-such a place," a place such that whoever went there would be killed and not return. He did so, and he was struck down. Dāwūd then proposed to her, and married her. [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/176; Tafsīr al-Ṣanʿānī: 3/161.]

Some said concerning the cause of that: Akhbarnā Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar al-Bāqirjī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlawiyyah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ismāʿīl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd ibn Bashīr from Qatādah from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd said to the Children of Israel when he became king: "By Allah, I will surely be just among you." He did not make the exception (by saying "in shāʾ Allāh"), so he was tested with it. [Zād al-Masīr: 6/326.]

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Warrāq said: The cause of that was that Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was much devoted to worship, and he was pleased with his knowledge, and said: "Is there anyone on earth who does my deeds?"

Then Jibrīl came to him and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: You have been pleased with your worship, and self-admiration devours worship. If you are pleased a second time, I will leave you to yourself."

He said: "My Lord, leave me to myself for a year."
He said: "Indeed it is a great deal."
He said: "Then an hour."
He said: "Then do as you will with it."

So he appointed guards, put on wool, entered the prayer niche (mihrab), and placed the Psalms (al-Zabur) before him. While he was in his devotion and worship, the bird suddenly landed before him, and what happened with the woman happened.

They said: When Dawud married the wife of Uriah, she had not stayed long before God, glory be to Him, sent two angels in the form of men. They asked to enter upon him, but they found him on his day of worship, and the guards prevented them from entering upon him. So they scaled the niche (mihrab) over him, and he did not notice until, while he was praying, they were sitting before him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/175.] This is His saying:

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche?﴾

They used a plural verb because "khasm" (adversary, litigant) is a noun that applies to the singular, the dual, and the plural, and to the masculine and the feminine alike.

Labid said:

*And adversaries who rush to enter, as if they were proud stallions, each bright-faced and well-bred...* [Lisan al-Arab: 12/180.]

Another poet said:

*And fierce adversaries who shake their beards, like the shaking of thoroughbred, well-bred horses...* [Fath al-Qadir: 4/425.]

The plural was used for the two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, so two and whatever is above them is a group, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].

Bal lammā (rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment; had they tasted it, they would not have said this). Am ʿindahum khazāʾinu raḥmati rabbika al-ʿazīzi al-wahhāb? (Or do they possess the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?) That is, the keys of prophethood; its parallel is in Surat al-Zukhruf: "Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?" [Q. 43:32], meaning the prophethood of your Lord. Am lahum mulku al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi wa mā baynahumā, falyartaqū fī al-asbāb? (Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend by the means.) That is, let them climb the mountains up to the heavens, and bring down revelation from there to whomever they choose and wish. This is a rebuke and a challenge to their incapacity.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mujāhid and Qatādah said: by "al-asbāb" is meant the gates of heaven and its paths.

Jundun mā hunālika mahzūmun min al-aḥzāb: they are an army there, defeated, prevented from ascending to the heavens, among the confederates (al-aḥzāb, the factions).

Most exegetes said: the meaning is that these chieftains who make this statement are a defeated, subdued army, while you (O Muhammad) are victorious and triumphant over them.

Qatādah said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised him in Makkah that He would defeat them, and its fulfilment came on the Day of Badr, [defeat of] the confederates, as with the earlier generations who were subdued and destroyed. Then He said, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ): Kadhdhabat qablahum qawmu Nūḥin wa ʿĀdun wa Firʿawnu dhū al-awtād. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "dhū al-awtād" means one of firm construction.

Al-Qutaybī said: The Arabs say, "They are in firmly-rooted might, and a firmly-rooted kingdom," meaning it is enduring and strong, and the origin of this is that a tent of theirs stands by its pegs (awtād).

Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said: "In the shade of a kingdom whose pegs are firm."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "dhū al-awtād" means possessor of strength and force.

Al-Ḥalabī and Muqātil said: He used to punish people with pegs. When he was angry with someone, he would stretch him out on his back between four pegs, each of his feet to a pillar and each of his hands to a pillar, and leave him thus suspended in the air between heaven and earth until he died.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: He would stretch the man out lying on the ground, then fasten him with pegs.

Al-Suddī said: He would stretch the man and fasten him with pegs, and send upon him scorpions and snakes.

Qatādah and ʿAṭāʾ said: He had pegs and cords (arsāl) and playthings (malāʿib) upon which he would amuse himself before his eyes.

Wa Thamūdu wa qawmu Lūṭin wa aṣḥābu al-Aykah, ulāʾika al-aḥzāb. In kullun illā kadhdhaba al-rusula fa-ḥaqqa ʿiqāb: each of them only denied the messengers, so My punishment became due and befell them.

Wa mā yanẓuru hāʾulāʾi, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan, which is the blast of the Resurrection.

This interpretation has been related traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mā lahā min fawāq.

Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: "from return." Al-Wālibī: "increase." Mujāhid: "a respite." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "rest."

There are two readings: fuwāq with a ḍamma on the fāʾ, the dialect of Tamīm, and the reading of Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf; and fawāq with a fatḥa, the dialect of Quraysh, the reading of the rest of the readers, and the choice of Abū ʿUbayd.

Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says ḥamām al-mukkūk and ḥamāmuhu, and qiṣāṣ al-shaʿr and qiṣāṣuhu. Others distinguished between them.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mu'arrikh said: with a fatḥa it means rest and recovery, like jawāb from ijābah, taking it to mean the patient's recovery from his illness; and al-fawāq with a ḍamma is the interval between two milkings, that is, one milks the she-camel, then leaves her for a while until the milk gathers; the interval between the two milkings is a fuwāq. It was then borrowed for the sense of waiting for a short period.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands guard for the interval of a she-camel's milking in the way of Allah, Allah forbids his body to the Fire." [Al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr of al-Suyūṭī: 2/603, no. 8692; Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 4/307, no. 10634.] [108]

Wa qālū rabbanā ʿajjil lanā qiṭṭanā qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: "that is, our book."

Also from him: "al-qiṭṭ is the scroll that has counted everything."

Abu al-ʿĀliyah and al-Kalbī said: when there was revealed in al-Ḥāqqah, "As for him who is given his book in his right hand" [Q. 69:19] and "As for him who is given his book in his left hand" [Q. 69:25].

They said, in mockery: "Hasten for us our qiṭṭ," meaning our book, hasten it for us in this world, qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: it means our punishment and what has been decreed for us of torment.

ʿAṭāʾ said: this was said by al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and it is his saying: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."

And he is the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall" [Q. 70:1]. ʿAṭāʾ said: some dozen verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning him.
