Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says ḥamām al-mukkūk and ḥamāmuhu, and qiṣāṣ al-shaʿr and qiṣāṣuhu. Others distinguished between them.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mu'arrikh said: with a fatḥa it means rest and recovery, like jawāb from ijābah, taking it to mean the patient's recovery from his illness; and al-fawāq with a ḍamma is the interval between two milkings, that is, one milks the she-camel, then leaves her for a while until the milk gathers; the interval between the two milkings is a fuwāq. It was then borrowed for the sense of waiting for a short period.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands guard for the interval of a she-camel's milking in the way of Allah, Allah forbids his body to the Fire." [Al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr of al-Suyūṭī: 2/603, no. 8692; Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 4/307, no. 10634.] [108]

Wa qālū rabbanā ʿajjil lanā qiṭṭanā qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: "that is, our book."

Also from him: "al-qiṭṭ is the scroll that has counted everything."

Abu al-ʿĀliyah and al-Kalbī said: when there was revealed in al-Ḥāqqah, "As for him who is given his book in his right hand" [Q. 69:19] and "As for him who is given his book in his left hand" [Q. 69:25].

They said, in mockery: "Hasten for us our qiṭṭ," meaning our book, hasten it for us in this world, qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: it means our punishment and what has been decreed for us of torment.

ʿAṭāʾ said: this was said by al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and it is his saying: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."

And he is the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall" [Q. 70:1]. ʿAṭāʾ said: some dozen verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning him.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they mean their share and portion of the Garden which is spoken of.

Al-Farrāʾ said: al-qiṭṭ in the speech of the Arabs means a share, and from it the written document (al-ṣakk) is called qiṭṭ.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: al-qiṭṭ is a book of gifts (bi-al-jawāʾah).

al-Aʿshā said:
"Nor the king al-Nuʿmān on the day I met him, giving with bounty the qiṭūṭ, and generous."

He means books of rewards, that is, with virtue and eminence. It is said a horse is afiq and a she-camel afiqah when they are noble and preferred over others.

Mujāhid said: qiṭṭanā means our reckoning, and the book of reckoning is called qiṭṭ; the root of the word is from writing.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Iṣbir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna, wa dhkur ʿabdanā Dāwūda dhā al-ayd: possessor of strength in worship. Innahu awwāb: obedient.

From Ibn ʿAbbās: returning repeatedly to repentance.

From al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: he is the one who glorifies (al-musabbiḥ) in the Ethiopian tongue.

Akhbarnī al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Dīnawarī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Faḍl ibn al-Faḍl al-Kindī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn [Fāris] in Baghdad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAmr ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from al-Zuhrī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Blueness is a sign of Yemen, and Dāwūd the Prophet (peace be upon him) was blue-eyed." [See: al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr: 2/33; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 6/17.] [109]

Innā sakhkharnā al-jibāla maʿahu yusabbiḥna: with his glorification.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: he used to understand the glorification of stone and tree.

Bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Shanbah, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn Yaḥyawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Umayyah Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I used to pass by this verse not knowing what al-ʿashiyy and al-ishrāq were, until Umm Hānīʾ bint Abī Ṭālib told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer, and said: 'O Umm Hānīʾ, this is the prayer of ishrāq.'" [110] [Musnad al-Ḥumaydī: 1/160; Musnad Ibn Rāhawayh: 5/19.]

ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There remained in my mind something about the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) until I sought it in the Qur'an and found it in this verse: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq."

ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿAbbās did not used to pray the forenoon prayer, and then he prayed it afterwards.

It is related that Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said to Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I find in the Book of Allah a prayer after the rising of the sun."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I will show you that in the Book of Allah, in the story of Dāwūd: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq; and al-ishrāq is not the rising of the sun, rather it is its clarity and brightness."

Wa al-ṭayra, that is, and We subjected the birds to him, maḥshūrah, gathered; kullun lahu, that is, to Dāwūd, awwāb, obedient. Wa shadadnā mulkahu, that is, We strengthened his kingdom.

Al-Ḥasan recited: wa shaddadnā with the doubling of the dāl.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was the mightiest of the kings of the earth in authority; every night thirty-three thousand men would guard his sanctuary (miḥrāb). That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom," through the guard.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man from the Children of Israel sought redress against a man of their notables, and the two came before the Prophet Dāwūd. The complainant said: "This man has seized my cow from me."

Dāwūd asked the man about it, and he denied it; he asked the other for proof, and he had no proof. Dāwūd said to them both: "Wait until I consider your affair."

They rose from his presence, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dāwūd (peace be upon him) in a dream that he should kill the man against whom redress was sought.

He said: "This is a dream, and I will not hasten until I am certain."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him a second time that he should kill him, but he did not do so. Allah revealed to him a third time: that he should kill him, or the punishment from Allah would come to him. Dāwūd sent for the man and said: "Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you."

The man said: "You would kill me without proof or certainty!" Dāwūd said: "Yes, by Allah, I will surely carry out the command of Allah concerning you."

When the man knew that he was about to kill him, he said: "Do not hasten until I tell you: by Allah, I was not seized for this sin, but I had secretly killed this man's father, and for that I have been seized."

Dāwūd then ordered him put to death, and his awe grew among the Children of Israel at that time for Dāwūd, and his kingdom became firm through it. That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom."

Wa ātaynāhu al-ḥikmah, that is, prophethood and correctness in affairs. Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: knowledge that the intellects do not reject.

Wa faṣla al-khiṭāb. Ibn ʿAbbās said: clarity of speech.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Kalbī, Ibn Masʿūd, Muqātil and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: it means the knowledge of judgment and insight into adjudication, such that he would not stammer in judging between people; and this is one of the reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: it is the proof upon the claimant and the oath upon the one who denies.

Akhbarnā Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Jawrī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Bakr Bālawayh ibn Muḥammad ibn Bālawayh al-Mirbatānī there, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Ḥawnī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Khamīṣamī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Aḥmad, who said: Akhbarnā Sharīk from al-Aʿmash from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Kaʿb regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths."

Anbaʾanī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid, who said: Akhbarnā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Ḥaddathanā Wahb ibn Jarīr, who said: Akhbarnā [Shuʿbah] from al-Ḥakam from Shurayḥ regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths." This is also the view of Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sumrah al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abī Shaybah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf al-Azraq from Zakariyyā, that is Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from [al-Subayʿī], who said: I heard Ziyād say: "Faṣla al-khiṭāb, which was given to Dāwūd, is 'amma baʿd,' and he was the first to say it."

Wa hal atāka naba' al-khaṣm (al-āyah). The scholars differed, in the reports of the prophets, concerning the reason Allah tested His Prophet Dāwūd with the sin with which he was tested.

Some people said: the cause of that was that one day he wished of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, the station of his forefathers Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb (peace be upon them), and asked that He test him in the manner in which He had tested them, and give him the bounty similar to what He had given them.

Al-Suddī, al-Kalbī and Muqātil related from their shaykhs, the narrations of some entering into others, they said: Dāwūd had divided time into three days: a day in which he judged between the people, a day in which he withdrew for the worship of his Lord, and a day in which he withdrew for his wives and his affairs. He found in what he read of the books the excellence of Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, and said:

"O Lord, all the good has been taken by my forefathers who came before me."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "They were tested with trials, with which you were not tested, and they were patient with them. Ibrāhīm was tested with Nimrod and with the slaughter of his son; Isḥāq was tested with being slaughtered and with the loss of his sight; Yaʿqūb was tested with grief over Yūsuf. And you have not been tested with any of that."

Dāwūd said: "My Lord, then test me with the like of what You tested them with, and give me the like of what You gave them."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "You will be tested in such-and-such a month, on such-and-such a day, so be on guard."

When that day which Allah had promised came, Dāwūd entered his sanctuary, closed its door, and began to pray and recite the Zabūr. While he was thus, Satan came to him in the form of a dove of gold with every beautiful color, and it fell between his feet. He stretched out his hand to take it and give it to a young son of his, but when he reached for it, it flew off not far away, without despairing him of itself; he extended his hand to take it, and it moved away, and he followed it, until it flew and landed in a window; he went to take it, and it flew out of the window. Dāwūd looked to see where it would fall, and he sent someone to catch it, and they saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. This is the saying of al-Kalbī.

Al-Suddī said: He saw her bathing on her roof, and he saw a woman of the most beautiful form, and Dāwūd marveled at her beauty. She turned, and saw his shadow, and she shook out her hair, which covered her body, and this increased his admiration for her, so he asked about her. It was said: she is Tashāyiʿ, daughter of Shāyiʿ, the wife of Uriyā ibn Ḥanānā, and her husband was on a campaign in al-Balqāʾ with Ayyūb ibn Ṣūriyā, the son of Dāwūd's sister.

Dāwūd wrote to his nephew Ayyūb, commander in al-Balqāʾ: "Send Uriyā to such-and-such a place, and put him forward before the Ark; and whoever is put forward before the Ark may not return behind it until Allah grants victory at his hands or he is martyred." So he sent him forward, and victory was granted at his hands, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, which is fiercer than that." He sent him, and victory was granted, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, fiercer in might than that." He sent him, and he was killed the third time. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dāwūd married her, and she is the mother of Sulaymān. [This story is a fable from which Allah keeps His friends, let alone His prophets; it appears in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/175; Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī: 1/338; and Mustadrak al-Ḥākim: 2/586.]

Others said: the cause of his trial was that his soul told him he could endure a day without committing any fault.

This is what Shuʿayb ibn Muḥammad informed us, who said: Akhbarnā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar, who said: Ḥaddathanā Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd from Maṭar from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd divided time into four parts: a day for his wives, a day for worship, a day for judging among the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, to remind them and be reminded by them, to make them weep and weep with them.

He said: When the day of the Children of Israel came, they mentioned and said: "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?"

Dāwūd resolved in himself that he would achieve that. When the day of his worship came, he locked his doors and ordered that no one enter upon him, and he devoted himself to reading the Torah. While he was reading, a golden dove with every beautiful color fell between his hands; he reached out to take it, but it flew and landed not far off, without despairing him of itself; he kept following it until he came upon a woman bathing; her form and beauty pleased him, and when she saw his shadow on the ground, she covered herself with her hair, which increased his admiration for her. He had sent her husband upon one of his armies, and he wrote to him: "Go to such-and-such a place," a place such that whoever went there would be killed and not return. He did so, and he was struck down. Dāwūd then proposed to her, and married her. [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/176; Tafsīr al-Ṣanʿānī: 3/161.]

Some said concerning the cause of that: Akhbarnā Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar al-Bāqirjī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlawiyyah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ismāʿīl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd ibn Bashīr from Qatādah from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd said to the Children of Israel when he became king: "By Allah, I will surely be just among you." He did not make the exception (by saying "in shāʾ Allāh"), so he was tested with it. [Zād al-Masīr: 6/326.]

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Warrāq said: The cause of that was that Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was much devoted to worship, and he was pleased with his knowledge, and said: "Is there anyone on earth who does my deeds?"

Then Jibrīl came to him and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: You have been pleased with your worship, and self-admiration devours worship. If you are pleased a second time, I will leave you to yourself."

He said: "My Lord, leave me to myself for a year."
He said: "Indeed it is a great deal."
He said: "Then an hour."
He said: "Then do as you will with it."

So he appointed guards, put on wool, entered the prayer niche (mihrab), and placed the Psalms (al-Zabur) before him. While he was in his devotion and worship, the bird suddenly landed before him, and what happened with the woman happened.

They said: When Dawud married the wife of Uriah, she had not stayed long before God, glory be to Him, sent two angels in the form of men. They asked to enter upon him, but they found him on his day of worship, and the guards prevented them from entering upon him. So they scaled the niche (mihrab) over him, and he did not notice until, while he was praying, they were sitting before him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/175.] This is His saying:

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche?﴾

They used a plural verb because "khasm" (adversary, litigant) is a noun that applies to the singular, the dual, and the plural, and to the masculine and the feminine alike.

Labid said:

*And adversaries who rush to enter, as if they were proud stallions, each bright-faced and well-bred...* [Lisan al-Arab: 12/180.]

Another poet said:

*And fierce adversaries who shake their beards, like the shaking of thoroughbred, well-bred horses...* [Fath al-Qadir: 4/425.]

The plural was used for the two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, so two and whatever is above them is a group, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].

Bal lammā (rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment; had they tasted it, they would not have said this). Am ʿindahum khazāʾinu raḥmati rabbika al-ʿazīzi al-wahhāb? (Or do they possess the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?) That is, the keys of prophethood; its parallel is in Surat al-Zukhruf: "Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?" [Q. 43:32], meaning the prophethood of your Lord. Am lahum mulku al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi wa mā baynahumā, falyartaqū fī al-asbāb? (Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend by the means.) That is, let them climb the mountains up to the heavens, and bring down revelation from there to whomever they choose and wish. This is a rebuke and a challenge to their incapacity.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mujāhid and Qatādah said: by "al-asbāb" is meant the gates of heaven and its paths.

Jundun mā hunālika mahzūmun min al-aḥzāb: they are an army there, defeated, prevented from ascending to the heavens, among the confederates (al-aḥzāb, the factions).

Most exegetes said: the meaning is that these chieftains who make this statement are a defeated, subdued army, while you (O Muhammad) are victorious and triumphant over them.

Qatādah said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised him in Makkah that He would defeat them, and its fulfilment came on the Day of Badr, [defeat of] the confederates, as with the earlier generations who were subdued and destroyed. Then He said, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ): Kadhdhabat qablahum qawmu Nūḥin wa ʿĀdun wa Firʿawnu dhū al-awtād. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "dhū al-awtād" means one of firm construction.

Al-Qutaybī said: The Arabs say, "They are in firmly-rooted might, and a firmly-rooted kingdom," meaning it is enduring and strong, and the origin of this is that a tent of theirs stands by its pegs (awtād).

Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said: "In the shade of a kingdom whose pegs are firm."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "dhū al-awtād" means possessor of strength and force.

Al-Ḥalabī and Muqātil said: He used to punish people with pegs. When he was angry with someone, he would stretch him out on his back between four pegs, each of his feet to a pillar and each of his hands to a pillar, and leave him thus suspended in the air between heaven and earth until he died.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: He would stretch the man out lying on the ground, then fasten him with pegs.

Al-Suddī said: He would stretch the man and fasten him with pegs, and send upon him scorpions and snakes.

Qatādah and ʿAṭāʾ said: He had pegs and cords (arsāl) and playthings (malāʿib) upon which he would amuse himself before his eyes.

Wa Thamūdu wa qawmu Lūṭin wa aṣḥābu al-Aykah, ulāʾika al-aḥzāb. In kullun illā kadhdhaba al-rusula fa-ḥaqqa ʿiqāb: each of them only denied the messengers, so My punishment became due and befell them.

Wa mā yanẓuru hāʾulāʾi, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan, which is the blast of the Resurrection.

This interpretation has been related traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mā lahā min fawāq.

Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: "from return." Al-Wālibī: "increase." Mujāhid: "a respite." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "rest."

There are two readings: fuwāq with a ḍamma on the fāʾ, the dialect of Tamīm, and the reading of Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf; and fawāq with a fatḥa, the dialect of Quraysh, the reading of the rest of the readers, and the choice of Abū ʿUbayd.

Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says ḥamām al-mukkūk and ḥamāmuhu, and qiṣāṣ al-shaʿr and qiṣāṣuhu. Others distinguished between them.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mu'arrikh said: with a fatḥa it means rest and recovery, like jawāb from ijābah, taking it to mean the patient's recovery from his illness; and al-fawāq with a ḍamma is the interval between two milkings, that is, one milks the she-camel, then leaves her for a while until the milk gathers; the interval between the two milkings is a fuwāq. It was then borrowed for the sense of waiting for a short period.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands guard for the interval of a she-camel's milking in the way of Allah, Allah forbids his body to the Fire." [Al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr of al-Suyūṭī: 2/603, no. 8692; Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 4/307, no. 10634.] [108]

Wa qālū rabbanā ʿajjil lanā qiṭṭanā qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: "that is, our book."

Also from him: "al-qiṭṭ is the scroll that has counted everything."

Abu al-ʿĀliyah and al-Kalbī said: when there was revealed in al-Ḥāqqah, "As for him who is given his book in his right hand" [Q. 69:19] and "As for him who is given his book in his left hand" [Q. 69:25].

They said, in mockery: "Hasten for us our qiṭṭ," meaning our book, hasten it for us in this world, qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: it means our punishment and what has been decreed for us of torment.

ʿAṭāʾ said: this was said by al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and it is his saying: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."

And he is the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall" [Q. 70:1]. ʿAṭāʾ said: some dozen verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning him.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they mean their share and portion of the Garden which is spoken of.

Al-Farrāʾ said: al-qiṭṭ in the speech of the Arabs means a share, and from it the written document (al-ṣakk) is called qiṭṭ.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: al-qiṭṭ is a book of gifts (bi-al-jawāʾah).

al-Aʿshā said:
"Nor the king al-Nuʿmān on the day I met him, giving with bounty the qiṭūṭ, and generous."

He means books of rewards, that is, with virtue and eminence. It is said a horse is afiq and a she-camel afiqah when they are noble and preferred over others.

Mujāhid said: qiṭṭanā means our reckoning, and the book of reckoning is called qiṭṭ; the root of the word is from writing.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Iṣbir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna, wa dhkur ʿabdanā Dāwūda dhā al-ayd: possessor of strength in worship. Innahu awwāb: obedient.

From Ibn ʿAbbās: returning repeatedly to repentance.

From al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: he is the one who glorifies (al-musabbiḥ) in the Ethiopian tongue.

Akhbarnī al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Dīnawarī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Faḍl ibn al-Faḍl al-Kindī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn [Fāris] in Baghdad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAmr ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from al-Zuhrī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Blueness is a sign of Yemen, and Dāwūd the Prophet (peace be upon him) was blue-eyed." [See: al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr: 2/33; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 6/17.] [109]

Innā sakhkharnā al-jibāla maʿahu yusabbiḥna: with his glorification.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: he used to understand the glorification of stone and tree.

Bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Shanbah, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn Yaḥyawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Umayyah Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I used to pass by this verse not knowing what al-ʿashiyy and al-ishrāq were, until Umm Hānīʾ bint Abī Ṭālib told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer, and said: 'O Umm Hānīʾ, this is the prayer of ishrāq.'" [110] [Musnad al-Ḥumaydī: 1/160; Musnad Ibn Rāhawayh: 5/19.]

ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There remained in my mind something about the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) until I sought it in the Qur'an and found it in this verse: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq."

ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿAbbās did not used to pray the forenoon prayer, and then he prayed it afterwards.

It is related that Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said to Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I find in the Book of Allah a prayer after the rising of the sun."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I will show you that in the Book of Allah, in the story of Dāwūd: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq; and al-ishrāq is not the rising of the sun, rather it is its clarity and brightness."

Wa al-ṭayra, that is, and We subjected the birds to him, maḥshūrah, gathered; kullun lahu, that is, to Dāwūd, awwāb, obedient. Wa shadadnā mulkahu, that is, We strengthened his kingdom.

Al-Ḥasan recited: wa shaddadnā with the doubling of the dāl.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was the mightiest of the kings of the earth in authority; every night thirty-three thousand men would guard his sanctuary (miḥrāb). That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom," through the guard.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man from the Children of Israel sought redress against a man of their notables, and the two came before the Prophet Dāwūd. The complainant said: "This man has seized my cow from me."

Dāwūd asked the man about it, and he denied it; he asked the other for proof, and he had no proof. Dāwūd said to them both: "Wait until I consider your affair."

They rose from his presence, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dāwūd (peace be upon him) in a dream that he should kill the man against whom redress was sought.

He said: "This is a dream, and I will not hasten until I am certain."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him a second time that he should kill him, but he did not do so. Allah revealed to him a third time: that he should kill him, or the punishment from Allah would come to him. Dāwūd sent for the man and said: "Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you."

The man said: "You would kill me without proof or certainty!" Dāwūd said: "Yes, by Allah, I will surely carry out the command of Allah concerning you."

When the man knew that he was about to kill him, he said: "Do not hasten until I tell you: by Allah, I was not seized for this sin, but I had secretly killed this man's father, and for that I have been seized."

Dāwūd then ordered him put to death, and his awe grew among the Children of Israel at that time for Dāwūd, and his kingdom became firm through it. That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom."

Wa ātaynāhu al-ḥikmah, that is, prophethood and correctness in affairs. Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: knowledge that the intellects do not reject.

Wa faṣla al-khiṭāb. Ibn ʿAbbās said: clarity of speech.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Kalbī, Ibn Masʿūd, Muqātil and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: it means the knowledge of judgment and insight into adjudication, such that he would not stammer in judging between people; and this is one of the reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: it is the proof upon the claimant and the oath upon the one who denies.

Akhbarnā Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Jawrī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Bakr Bālawayh ibn Muḥammad ibn Bālawayh al-Mirbatānī there, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Ḥawnī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Khamīṣamī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Aḥmad, who said: Akhbarnā Sharīk from al-Aʿmash from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Kaʿb regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths."

Anbaʾanī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid, who said: Akhbarnā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Ḥaddathanā Wahb ibn Jarīr, who said: Akhbarnā [Shuʿbah] from al-Ḥakam from Shurayḥ regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths." This is also the view of Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sumrah al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abī Shaybah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf al-Azraq from Zakariyyā, that is Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from [al-Subayʿī], who said: I heard Ziyād say: "Faṣla al-khiṭāb, which was given to Dāwūd, is 'amma baʿd,' and he was the first to say it."

Wa hal atāka naba' al-khaṣm (al-āyah). The scholars differed, in the reports of the prophets, concerning the reason Allah tested His Prophet Dāwūd with the sin with which he was tested.

Some people said: the cause of that was that one day he wished of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, the station of his forefathers Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb (peace be upon them), and asked that He test him in the manner in which He had tested them, and give him the bounty similar to what He had given them.

Al-Suddī, al-Kalbī and Muqātil related from their shaykhs, the narrations of some entering into others, they said: Dāwūd had divided time into three days: a day in which he judged between the people, a day in which he withdrew for the worship of his Lord, and a day in which he withdrew for his wives and his affairs. He found in what he read of the books the excellence of Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, and said:

"O Lord, all the good has been taken by my forefathers who came before me."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "They were tested with trials, with which you were not tested, and they were patient with them. Ibrāhīm was tested with Nimrod and with the slaughter of his son; Isḥāq was tested with being slaughtered and with the loss of his sight; Yaʿqūb was tested with grief over Yūsuf. And you have not been tested with any of that."

Dāwūd said: "My Lord, then test me with the like of what You tested them with, and give me the like of what You gave them."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "You will be tested in such-and-such a month, on such-and-such a day, so be on guard."

When that day which Allah had promised came, Dāwūd entered his sanctuary, closed its door, and began to pray and recite the Zabūr. While he was thus, Satan came to him in the form of a dove of gold with every beautiful color, and it fell between his feet. He stretched out his hand to take it and give it to a young son of his, but when he reached for it, it flew off not far away, without despairing him of itself; he extended his hand to take it, and it moved away, and he followed it, until it flew and landed in a window; he went to take it, and it flew out of the window. Dāwūd looked to see where it would fall, and he sent someone to catch it, and they saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. This is the saying of al-Kalbī.

Al-Suddī said: He saw her bathing on her roof, and he saw a woman of the most beautiful form, and Dāwūd marveled at her beauty. She turned, and saw his shadow, and she shook out her hair, which covered her body, and this increased his admiration for her, so he asked about her. It was said: she is Tashāyiʿ, daughter of Shāyiʿ, the wife of Uriyā ibn Ḥanānā, and her husband was on a campaign in al-Balqāʾ with Ayyūb ibn Ṣūriyā, the son of Dāwūd's sister.

Dāwūd wrote to his nephew Ayyūb, commander in al-Balqāʾ: "Send Uriyā to such-and-such a place, and put him forward before the Ark; and whoever is put forward before the Ark may not return behind it until Allah grants victory at his hands or he is martyred." So he sent him forward, and victory was granted at his hands, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, which is fiercer than that." He sent him, and victory was granted, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, fiercer in might than that." He sent him, and he was killed the third time. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dāwūd married her, and she is the mother of Sulaymān. [This story is a fable from which Allah keeps His friends, let alone His prophets; it appears in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/175; Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī: 1/338; and Mustadrak al-Ḥākim: 2/586.]

Others said: the cause of his trial was that his soul told him he could endure a day without committing any fault.

This is what Shuʿayb ibn Muḥammad informed us, who said: Akhbarnā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar, who said: Ḥaddathanā Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd from Maṭar from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd divided time into four parts: a day for his wives, a day for worship, a day for judging among the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, to remind them and be reminded by them, to make them weep and weep with them.

He said: When the day of the Children of Israel came, they mentioned and said: "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?"

Dāwūd resolved in himself that he would achieve that. When the day of his worship came, he locked his doors and ordered that no one enter upon him, and he devoted himself to reading the Torah. While he was reading, a golden dove with every beautiful color fell between his hands; he reached out to take it, but it flew and landed not far off, without despairing him of itself; he kept following it until he came upon a woman bathing; her form and beauty pleased him, and when she saw his shadow on the ground, she covered herself with her hair, which increased his admiration for her. He had sent her husband upon one of his armies, and he wrote to him: "Go to such-and-such a place," a place such that whoever went there would be killed and not return. He did so, and he was struck down. Dāwūd then proposed to her, and married her. [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/176; Tafsīr al-Ṣanʿānī: 3/161.]

Some said concerning the cause of that: Akhbarnā Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar al-Bāqirjī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlawiyyah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ismāʿīl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd ibn Bashīr from Qatādah from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd said to the Children of Israel when he became king: "By Allah, I will surely be just among you." He did not make the exception (by saying "in shāʾ Allāh"), so he was tested with it. [Zād al-Masīr: 6/326.]

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Warrāq said: The cause of that was that Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was much devoted to worship, and he was pleased with his knowledge, and said: "Is there anyone on earth who does my deeds?"

Then Jibrīl came to him and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: You have been pleased with your worship, and self-admiration devours worship. If you are pleased a second time, I will leave you to yourself."

He said: "My Lord, leave me to myself for a year."
He said: "Indeed it is a great deal."
He said: "Then an hour."
He said: "Then do as you will with it."

So he appointed guards, put on wool, entered the prayer niche (mihrab), and placed the Psalms (al-Zabur) before him. While he was in his devotion and worship, the bird suddenly landed before him, and what happened with the woman happened.

They said: When Dawud married the wife of Uriah, she had not stayed long before God, glory be to Him, sent two angels in the form of men. They asked to enter upon him, but they found him on his day of worship, and the guards prevented them from entering upon him. So they scaled the niche (mihrab) over him, and he did not notice until, while he was praying, they were sitting before him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/175.] This is His saying:

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche?﴾

They used a plural verb because "khasm" (adversary, litigant) is a noun that applies to the singular, the dual, and the plural, and to the masculine and the feminine alike.

Labid said:

*And adversaries who rush to enter, as if they were proud stallions, each bright-faced and well-bred...* [Lisan al-Arab: 12/180.]

Another poet said:

*And fierce adversaries who shake their beards, like the shaking of thoroughbred, well-bred horses...* [Fath al-Qadir: 4/425.]

The plural was used for the two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, so two and whatever is above them is a group, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].

Bal lammā (rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment; had they tasted it, they would not have said this). Am ʿindahum khazāʾinu raḥmati rabbika al-ʿazīzi al-wahhāb? (Or do they possess the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?) That is, the keys of prophethood; its parallel is in Surat al-Zukhruf: "Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?" [Q. 43:32], meaning the prophethood of your Lord. Am lahum mulku al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi wa mā baynahumā, falyartaqū fī al-asbāb? (Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend by the means.) That is, let them climb the mountains up to the heavens, and bring down revelation from there to whomever they choose and wish. This is a rebuke and a challenge to their incapacity.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mujāhid and Qatādah said: by "al-asbāb" is meant the gates of heaven and its paths.

Jundun mā hunālika mahzūmun min al-aḥzāb: they are an army there, defeated, prevented from ascending to the heavens, among the confederates (al-aḥzāb, the factions).

Most exegetes said: the meaning is that these chieftains who make this statement are a defeated, subdued army, while you (O Muhammad) are victorious and triumphant over them.

Qatādah said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised him in Makkah that He would defeat them, and its fulfilment came on the Day of Badr, [defeat of] the confederates, as with the earlier generations who were subdued and destroyed. Then He said, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ): Kadhdhabat qablahum qawmu Nūḥin wa ʿĀdun wa Firʿawnu dhū al-awtād. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "dhū al-awtād" means one of firm construction.

Al-Qutaybī said: The Arabs say, "They are in firmly-rooted might, and a firmly-rooted kingdom," meaning it is enduring and strong, and the origin of this is that a tent of theirs stands by its pegs (awtād).

Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said: "In the shade of a kingdom whose pegs are firm."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "dhū al-awtād" means possessor of strength and force.

Al-Ḥalabī and Muqātil said: He used to punish people with pegs. When he was angry with someone, he would stretch him out on his back between four pegs, each of his feet to a pillar and each of his hands to a pillar, and leave him thus suspended in the air between heaven and earth until he died.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: He would stretch the man out lying on the ground, then fasten him with pegs.

Al-Suddī said: He would stretch the man and fasten him with pegs, and send upon him scorpions and snakes.

Qatādah and ʿAṭāʾ said: He had pegs and cords (arsāl) and playthings (malāʿib) upon which he would amuse himself before his eyes.

Wa Thamūdu wa qawmu Lūṭin wa aṣḥābu al-Aykah, ulāʾika al-aḥzāb. In kullun illā kadhdhaba al-rusula fa-ḥaqqa ʿiqāb: each of them only denied the messengers, so My punishment became due and befell them.

Wa mā yanẓuru hāʾulāʾi, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah, illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan, which is the blast of the Resurrection.

This interpretation has been related traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mā lahā min fawāq.

Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: "from return." Al-Wālibī: "increase." Mujāhid: "a respite." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "rest."

There are two readings: fuwāq with a ḍamma on the fāʾ, the dialect of Tamīm, and the reading of Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf; and fawāq with a fatḥa, the dialect of Quraysh, the reading of the rest of the readers, and the choice of Abū ʿUbayd.

Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialects with one meaning, as one says ḥamām al-mukkūk and ḥamāmuhu, and qiṣāṣ al-shaʿr and qiṣāṣuhu. Others distinguished between them.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mu'arrikh said: with a fatḥa it means rest and recovery, like jawāb from ijābah, taking it to mean the patient's recovery from his illness; and al-fawāq with a ḍamma is the interval between two milkings, that is, one milks the she-camel, then leaves her for a while until the milk gathers; the interval between the two milkings is a fuwāq. It was then borrowed for the sense of waiting for a short period.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands guard for the interval of a she-camel's milking in the way of Allah, Allah forbids his body to the Fire." [Al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr of al-Suyūṭī: 2/603, no. 8692; Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 4/307, no. 10634.] [108]

Wa qālū rabbanā ʿajjil lanā qiṭṭanā qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: "that is, our book."

Also from him: "al-qiṭṭ is the scroll that has counted everything."

Abu al-ʿĀliyah and al-Kalbī said: when there was revealed in al-Ḥāqqah, "As for him who is given his book in his right hand" [Q. 69:19] and "As for him who is given his book in his left hand" [Q. 69:25].

They said, in mockery: "Hasten for us our qiṭṭ," meaning our book, hasten it for us in this world, qabla yawmi al-ḥisāb.

Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, Mujāhid and al-Suddī said: it means our punishment and what has been decreed for us of torment.

ʿAṭāʾ said: this was said by al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and it is his saying: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."

And he is the one of whom Allah, the Exalted, said: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall" [Q. 70:1]. ʿAṭāʾ said: some dozen verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning him.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they mean their share and portion of the Garden which is spoken of.

Al-Farrāʾ said: al-qiṭṭ in the speech of the Arabs means a share, and from it the written document (al-ṣakk) is called qiṭṭ.

Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: al-qiṭṭ is a book of gifts (bi-al-jawāʾah).

al-Aʿshā said:
"Nor the king al-Nuʿmān on the day I met him, giving with bounty the qiṭūṭ, and generous."

He means books of rewards, that is, with virtue and eminence. It is said a horse is afiq and a she-camel afiqah when they are noble and preferred over others.

Mujāhid said: qiṭṭanā means our reckoning, and the book of reckoning is called qiṭṭ; the root of the word is from writing.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Iṣbir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna, wa dhkur ʿabdanā Dāwūda dhā al-ayd: possessor of strength in worship. Innahu awwāb: obedient.

From Ibn ʿAbbās: returning repeatedly to repentance.

From al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: he is the one who glorifies (al-musabbiḥ) in the Ethiopian tongue.

Akhbarnī al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Dīnawarī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Faḍl ibn al-Faḍl al-Kindī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn [Fāris] in Baghdad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAmr ibn Ḥuṣayn, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAmr from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from al-Zuhrī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Blueness is a sign of Yemen, and Dāwūd the Prophet (peace be upon him) was blue-eyed." [See: al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaghīr: 2/33; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 6/17.] [109]

Innā sakhkharnā al-jibāla maʿahu yusabbiḥna: with his glorification.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: he used to understand the glorification of stone and tree.

Bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Shanbah, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn Yaḥyawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Umayyah Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I used to pass by this verse not knowing what al-ʿashiyy and al-ishrāq were, until Umm Hānīʾ bint Abī Ṭālib told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, asked for water for ablution, performed ablution, then prayed the forenoon prayer, and said: 'O Umm Hānīʾ, this is the prayer of ishrāq.'" [110] [Musnad al-Ḥumaydī: 1/160; Musnad Ibn Rāhawayh: 5/19.]

ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There remained in my mind something about the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) until I sought it in the Qur'an and found it in this verse: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq."

ʿIkrimah said: Ibn ʿAbbās did not used to pray the forenoon prayer, and then he prayed it afterwards.

It is related that Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said to Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I find in the Book of Allah a prayer after the rising of the sun."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I will show you that in the Book of Allah, in the story of Dāwūd: yusabbiḥna bi-al-ʿashiyyi wa al-ishrāq; and al-ishrāq is not the rising of the sun, rather it is its clarity and brightness."

Wa al-ṭayra, that is, and We subjected the birds to him, maḥshūrah, gathered; kullun lahu, that is, to Dāwūd, awwāb, obedient. Wa shadadnā mulkahu, that is, We strengthened his kingdom.

Al-Ḥasan recited: wa shaddadnā with the doubling of the dāl.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: He was the mightiest of the kings of the earth in authority; every night thirty-three thousand men would guard his sanctuary (miḥrāb). That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom," through the guard.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed us, who said: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn al-Ḥasan informed us, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad from ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās: that a man from the Children of Israel sought redress against a man of their notables, and the two came before the Prophet Dāwūd. The complainant said: "This man has seized my cow from me."

Dāwūd asked the man about it, and he denied it; he asked the other for proof, and he had no proof. Dāwūd said to them both: "Wait until I consider your affair."

They rose from his presence, and Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dāwūd (peace be upon him) in a dream that he should kill the man against whom redress was sought.

He said: "This is a dream, and I will not hasten until I am certain."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him a second time that he should kill him, but he did not do so. Allah revealed to him a third time: that he should kill him, or the punishment from Allah would come to him. Dāwūd sent for the man and said: "Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you."

The man said: "You would kill me without proof or certainty!" Dāwūd said: "Yes, by Allah, I will surely carry out the command of Allah concerning you."

When the man knew that he was about to kill him, he said: "Do not hasten until I tell you: by Allah, I was not seized for this sin, but I had secretly killed this man's father, and for that I have been seized."

Dāwūd then ordered him put to death, and his awe grew among the Children of Israel at that time for Dāwūd, and his kingdom became firm through it. That is His saying: "And We strengthened his kingdom."

Wa ātaynāhu al-ḥikmah, that is, prophethood and correctness in affairs. Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: knowledge that the intellects do not reject.

Wa faṣla al-khiṭāb. Ibn ʿAbbās said: clarity of speech.

Al-Ḥasan, al-Kalbī, Ibn Masʿūd, Muqātil and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: it means the knowledge of judgment and insight into adjudication, such that he would not stammer in judging between people; and this is one of the reports from Ibn ʿAbbās.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: it is the proof upon the claimant and the oath upon the one who denies.

Akhbarnā Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Jawrī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Bakr Bālawayh ibn Muḥammad ibn Bālawayh al-Mirbatānī there, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Ḥawnī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Khamīṣamī, who said: Akhbarnā Abū Aḥmad, who said: Akhbarnā Sharīk from al-Aʿmash from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Kaʿb regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths."

Anbaʾanī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid, who said: Akhbarnā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: Ḥaddathanā Wahb ibn Jarīr, who said: Akhbarnā [Shuʿbah] from al-Ḥakam from Shurayḥ regarding His saying "wa faṣla al-khiṭāb": "the witnesses and the oaths." This is also the view of Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ.

Akhbarnī Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sumrah al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abī Shaybah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Baghawī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf al-Azraq from Zakariyyā, that is Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, from [al-Subayʿī], who said: I heard Ziyād say: "Faṣla al-khiṭāb, which was given to Dāwūd, is 'amma baʿd,' and he was the first to say it."

Wa hal atāka naba' al-khaṣm (al-āyah). The scholars differed, in the reports of the prophets, concerning the reason Allah tested His Prophet Dāwūd with the sin with which he was tested.

Some people said: the cause of that was that one day he wished of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, the station of his forefathers Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb (peace be upon them), and asked that He test him in the manner in which He had tested them, and give him the bounty similar to what He had given them.

Al-Suddī, al-Kalbī and Muqātil related from their shaykhs, the narrations of some entering into others, they said: Dāwūd had divided time into three days: a day in which he judged between the people, a day in which he withdrew for the worship of his Lord, and a day in which he withdrew for his wives and his affairs. He found in what he read of the books the excellence of Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, and said:

"O Lord, all the good has been taken by my forefathers who came before me."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "They were tested with trials, with which you were not tested, and they were patient with them. Ibrāhīm was tested with Nimrod and with the slaughter of his son; Isḥāq was tested with being slaughtered and with the loss of his sight; Yaʿqūb was tested with grief over Yūsuf. And you have not been tested with any of that."

Dāwūd said: "My Lord, then test me with the like of what You tested them with, and give me the like of what You gave them."

Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "You will be tested in such-and-such a month, on such-and-such a day, so be on guard."

When that day which Allah had promised came, Dāwūd entered his sanctuary, closed its door, and began to pray and recite the Zabūr. While he was thus, Satan came to him in the form of a dove of gold with every beautiful color, and it fell between his feet. He stretched out his hand to take it and give it to a young son of his, but when he reached for it, it flew off not far away, without despairing him of itself; he extended his hand to take it, and it moved away, and he followed it, until it flew and landed in a window; he went to take it, and it flew out of the window. Dāwūd looked to see where it would fall, and he sent someone to catch it, and they saw a woman in a garden by the edge of a pool of hers, bathing. This is the saying of al-Kalbī.

Al-Suddī said: He saw her bathing on her roof, and he saw a woman of the most beautiful form, and Dāwūd marveled at her beauty. She turned, and saw his shadow, and she shook out her hair, which covered her body, and this increased his admiration for her, so he asked about her. It was said: she is Tashāyiʿ, daughter of Shāyiʿ, the wife of Uriyā ibn Ḥanānā, and her husband was on a campaign in al-Balqāʾ with Ayyūb ibn Ṣūriyā, the son of Dāwūd's sister.

Dāwūd wrote to his nephew Ayyūb, commander in al-Balqāʾ: "Send Uriyā to such-and-such a place, and put him forward before the Ark; and whoever is put forward before the Ark may not return behind it until Allah grants victory at his hands or he is martyred." So he sent him forward, and victory was granted at his hands, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, which is fiercer than that." He sent him, and victory was granted, and he wrote to Dāwūd about it; Dāwūd wrote to him again: "Send him to the enemy of such-and-such, fiercer in might than that." He sent him, and he was killed the third time. When the woman's waiting period ended, Dāwūd married her, and she is the mother of Sulaymān. [This story is a fable from which Allah keeps His friends, let alone His prophets; it appears in Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/175; Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī: 1/338; and Mustadrak al-Ḥākim: 2/586.]

Others said: the cause of his trial was that his soul told him he could endure a day without committing any fault.

This is what Shuʿayb ibn Muḥammad informed us, who said: Akhbarnā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn al-Azhar, who said: Ḥaddathanā Rawḥ ibn ʿUbādah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd from Maṭar from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd divided time into four parts: a day for his wives, a day for worship, a day for judging among the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, to remind them and be reminded by them, to make them weep and weep with them.

He said: When the day of the Children of Israel came, they mentioned and said: "Can there come upon a person a day in which he commits no sin?"

Dāwūd resolved in himself that he would achieve that. When the day of his worship came, he locked his doors and ordered that no one enter upon him, and he devoted himself to reading the Torah. While he was reading, a golden dove with every beautiful color fell between his hands; he reached out to take it, but it flew and landed not far off, without despairing him of itself; he kept following it until he came upon a woman bathing; her form and beauty pleased him, and when she saw his shadow on the ground, she covered herself with her hair, which increased his admiration for her. He had sent her husband upon one of his armies, and he wrote to him: "Go to such-and-such a place," a place such that whoever went there would be killed and not return. He did so, and he was struck down. Dāwūd then proposed to her, and married her. [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 23/176; Tafsīr al-Ṣanʿānī: 3/161.]

Some said concerning the cause of that: Akhbarnā Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥaddathanā Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar al-Bāqirjī, who said: Ḥaddathanā al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlawiyyah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ismāʿīl, who said: Ḥaddathanā Isḥāq, who said: Ḥaddathanā Saʿīd ibn Bashīr from Qatādah from al-Ḥasan, who said: Dāwūd said to the Children of Israel when he became king: "By Allah, I will surely be just among you." He did not make the exception (by saying "in shāʾ Allāh"), so he was tested with it. [Zād al-Masīr: 6/326.]

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Warrāq said: The cause of that was that Dāwūd (peace be upon him) was much devoted to worship, and he was pleased with his knowledge, and said: "Is there anyone on earth who does my deeds?"

Then Jibrīl came to him and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: You have been pleased with your worship, and self-admiration devours worship. If you are pleased a second time, I will leave you to yourself."

He said: "My Lord, leave me to myself for a year."
He said: "Indeed it is a great deal."
He said: "Then an hour."
He said: "Then do as you will with it."

So he appointed guards, put on wool, entered the prayer niche (mihrab), and placed the Psalms (al-Zabur) before him. While he was in his devotion and worship, the bird suddenly landed before him, and what happened with the woman happened.

They said: When Dawud married the wife of Uriah, she had not stayed long before God, glory be to Him, sent two angels in the form of men. They asked to enter upon him, but they found him on his day of worship, and the guards prevented them from entering upon him. So they scaled the niche (mihrab) over him, and he did not notice until, while he was praying, they were sitting before him. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/175.] This is His saying:

﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche?﴾

They used a plural verb because "khasm" (adversary, litigant) is a noun that applies to the singular, the dual, and the plural, and to the masculine and the feminine alike.

Labid said:

*And adversaries who rush to enter, as if they were proud stallions, each bright-faced and well-bred...* [Lisan al-Arab: 12/180.]

Another poet said:

*And fierce adversaries who shake their beards, like the shaking of thoroughbred, well-bred horses...* [Fath al-Qadir: 4/425.]

The plural was used for the two, because the meaning of plurality is the joining of one thing to another, so two and whatever is above them is a group, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 38, verses 22–28 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿When they entered upon Dawud﴾. Al-Farra' said: He has repeated "when" (idh) twice, and their meaning is as one, as when you say: "I struck you when you entered upon me, when you became bold." So the entering is the boldness. It is also permissible to make one of the two carry the sense of "lamma" (when).

﴿He was startled by them, when they climbed over the prayer niche (mihrab) to him without his permission.﴾

﴿They said: "Do not fear, O Dawud. We are two disputants, one of whom has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth, and do not be unjust (tushtit), and guide us to the even path.﴾ That is, we are two disputants, one of whom has transgressed against the other. "Judge between us with truth" and "do not be unjust (la tushtit) and do not deviate," related from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak.

al-Suddi said: "Do not be excessive (la tusrif)." Al-Mu'arrikh (the historian) said: "Do not be negligent (la tufarrit)."

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi recited: "wa la tashtut" (with a fatha on the ta' and a damma on the first ta'). Al-shatt and al-ashtat mean exceeding the limit. The root of the word is from "shatta al-dar" (the house was far away) and "ashatta" (it became distant).

﴿and guide us to the even path﴾, that is, the middle of the road.

If it is asked: How did he say ﴿This is my brother﴾, thereby making them brothers, when there is no kinship between the angels, since they do not beget offspring?

The answer: The meaning of the verse is "We are two disputants," as one says, "his face: the moon for beauty," meaning "like the moon." ﴿One of the two disputants said: "This is my brother"﴾ is by way of illustration (tamthil), not literal fact, meaning that the two are on one path and of one kind, as in His statement, glorified is He: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾. It has been said that the two who climbed over were two brothers from the Children of Israel, the same father and mother, and that one of them was a king and the other was not a king, so Dawud was alerted to what had been done.

﴿He has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe.﴾ This is one of the finest forms of allusion (ta'rid), to the point that he referred to women by ewes. The Arabs do this often, veiling their reference to women by gazelles, sheep, and cows, and it is frequent and clearer in their poetry.

al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: This is an allusion for warning and making understood, because there were no ewes and no transgression there. It is like people saying "Zayd struck 'Amr," "'Amr wronged Zayd," and "Bakr bought a house," when there was no striking, no wronging, and no buying.

﴿So he said: "Entrust it to me (akfilnihā)."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Give it to me." Ibn Jubayr related from him: "Transfer it to me." Mujahid said: "Let it come down to me." Abu al-'Aliya said: "Add it to me so that I may take charge of it." Ibn Kaysan said: "Make it my share (kafl), that is, my portion."

﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾, that is, he prevailed over me in argument.

al-Dahhak said: "If he speaks, he is more eloquent than I, and if he fights, he is more forceful than I."

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr recited: "wa 'azzani fi al-khitab" with an alif (wa 'azzani), from al-mu'azz, which is contention.

﴿He (Dawud) said: "He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe to add to his ewes."﴾ If it is asked: How was it permissible for Dawud to judge when he had not heard the words of the other disputant?

It is said: The meaning of the verse is that when one of them made a claim against the other, his companion was identified to him. Upon his acknowledgment, he decided the case with his words, "He has certainly wronged you." So the acknowledgment is omitted, because the apparent sense of the verse indicates it, like the Arabs' saying: "I commanded you to trade, so you gained wealth."

The poet said:

"My daughter said, when she saw me pale,
'It is as if you were a happy man whom food keeps well; a physician...'
Events followed one another, bringing down my brothers,
so they whitened my head, and calamities whiten."

﴿And indeed many of the partners (khulata') oppress one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they﴾, so they are not like that. This is the evidence for what we have mentioned of the interpretation.

What al-Suddi related with his chain: When one of them said, "This is my brother," and the rest of the verse, Dawud said to the other: "What do you say?" He said: "I have ninety-nine ewes, and my brother here has one ewe, and I want to take it from him so that my ewes become a hundred." He said: "And he was unwilling."

He (Dawud) said: "Then we will not leave you to that. And if you attempt it, we will strike this and this and this," meaning the tip of the nose, and its origin is the forehead.

He said: "O Dawud, you have more right to be struck, this and this, since you have ninety-nine women, while Uriyah had only one woman." So he kept at him, making him face death, until he was killed, and his wife was married (to Dawud).

He said: Dawud looked and saw no one, so he knew what he had fallen into. This is His statement, glorified is He: ﴿And Dawud thought (wa zanna) and became certain that We had tested him (fatannahu)﴾, meaning We had tried him.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The trial of Dawud was only a glance."

I say: Dawud did not deliberately look at the woman, but he looked at her again, and so she came to be upon him.

These are the sayings of the early generation (al-salaf) among the people of tafsir concerning the story of Dawud's trial.

It is related from al-Harith al-A'war, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Whoever narrates the story of Dawud according to what the storytellers (al-qussas) relate, believing it to be true, I will flog him two hundred lashes, for the magnitude of what he has committed and the greatness of the sin and wrongdoing he has bequeathed, by attributing to one whom Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has raised in station and made clear as a mercy to the worlds and a proof for the guided.

Those who uphold the exoneration of the messengers (al-munazzihin) regarding this story said: The sin of Dawud was that he wished the wife of Uriyah were lawful to him, and he entertained the thought of sin. It happened that Uriyah went out to war and advanced in the battle and was killed. When news of his death reached Dawud, he did not grieve for him or show sorrow for him, as he would have grieved for others of his soldiers when they perished. Then he married his wife. So Allah, glorified is He, rebuked him for that, because the sins of the prophets, however small they are, are great in the sight of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

Some of them said: The sin of Dawud was that Uriyah had proposed to that woman and had set his heart on her. When he was absent on his military expedition, Dawud proposed to her, and she was married to him because of his high station. Uriyah was greatly grieved by that, so Allah, exalted is He, rebuked him for that, since that one woman was not to be left for her first suitor, when he already had ninety-nine women.

Among what confirms what we have mentioned is what was said by the earlier exegetes, namely what:

'Aqil ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed me that al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya, the judge in Baghdad, Ahmad ibn Zakariyya, told him from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told me, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told me, from Abu Sakhr, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, that he heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say:

"When Dawud the Prophet looked at the woman and was inclined toward her, he ordered a force for the Children of Israel, and he instructed the commander of the expedition, saying: 'When the enemy is present, bring forward So-and-so before the Ark.' In that time, whoever was sent before the Ark was sought for victory by means of it, and the Ark would not turn back until the one sent before it was killed or the army fled from it. So the husband of the woman was killed, and the commander came to Dawud, relating to him his account. Dawud perceived (the matter) and fell prostrate. He remained for forty nights prostrating, until the crops grew from his tears, and the termites ate from his forehead. He was saying in his prostration: 'My Lord, Dawud has slipped in a slip farther than the distance between the east and the west. My Lord, if You do not have mercy on the weakness of Dawud and forgive his sin, You will make his sin a tale among those who come after him.'

Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him after forty nights and said: 'O Dawud, Allah has forgiven you the concern you had.'

Dawud said: 'I know that the Lord is able to forgive me the concern I had, and I know that Allah is just and does not incline. So how about So-and-so, when he comes on the Day of Resurrection and says: "My Lord, my blood that is with Dawud"?'

Jibril said: 'I did not ask your Lord about that, but if you wish, I will do it.'

He said: 'Yes.'

Jibril ascended, and Dawud prostrated and remained as long as Allah willed. Then he descended and said: 'O Dawud, I asked Allah, exalted is He, about that for which you sent me, and He said: "Tell Dawud that Allah will gather you both on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say to him: 'Grant me your blood which is with Dawud.' He will say: 'It is yours, O Lord.' Then He will say: 'For you in Paradise is whatever you wish and desire, as a recompense.'"'"

It was also related to me by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: al-Baqarji told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyya told us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, saying: Juwaybir and Muqatil informed us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: And Sa'id ibn Bashir and 'Isma ibn Hadas al-Qatti informed us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan and Ibn Sam'an, from one who related to him from Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: And Abu al-Ilyas informed me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih. They all said:

When the two angels entered upon Dawud and he passed judgment against himself, they changed into their forms and ascended, saying: "The man has passed judgment against himself." Dawud knew that it was about him, so he fell prostrate for forty days, not raising his head except for a need or for the time of an obligatory prayer. Then he would return to prostration, and he would not raise his head except for a need that could not be avoided, then return and prostrate again, for the full forty days, eating nothing and drinking nothing, weeping, until the crops grew around his head. He was calling upon his Lord, mighty and majestic, and asking Him for repentance. He was saying in his prostration:

"Glory be to the Mighty King, who tests creation with whatever He wills. Glory be to the Creator of light. Glory be to the One who comes between hearts. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, You left me and my enemy Iblis, and I did not stand firm against his temptation when it descended upon me. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, the bereaved mother weeps over her child when she loses him, and Dawud weeps over his sin. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, I was not admonished by what You admonished others with. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, You created me, and in Your eternal knowledge was what I would come to. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, a garment is washed and its dirt and filth depart, but sin clings to me and does not depart from me. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, You commanded me to be to the orphan like a merciful father, and to the widow like a merciful husband, but I forgot Your covenant. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, woe to Dawud when the veil is removed from him and it is said: 'This is Dawud the sinner.' Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, with which eyes will I look at You on the Day of Resurrection, when the wrongdoers only look sidelong? My God, with which foot will I stand before You on the day when the feet of sinners slip? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, woe to sinners on the Day of Resurrection because of the evil of reckoning. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, the stars passed and I knew them by their names, yet You left me while sin clings to me. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, from where does one seek forgiveness except from his Master? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, the sky rained but did not rain around me. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, the earth grew green but did not grow green around me because of my sin. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, I am one who cannot bear the heat of Your sun, so how can I bear the heat of Your fire? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, I am one who cannot bear the sound of Your thunder, so how can I bear the sound of Hell? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, how do sinners hide themselves from You through their sins, while You are witnessing them wherever they are? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, my forehead has been wounded and my eyes have dried up from fear of the burning upon my body. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, the birds glorify You with weak voices, fearing You, while I am the sinful servant who did not keep Your commandment. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, woe to Dawud because of the great sin he committed. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, You are the Helper, and I am the one seeking help, so who would the one seeking help call upon except the Helper? Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, You know my secret and my open affairs, so accept my excuse. Glory be to the Creator of light.

O Allah, I ask You, the God of Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, and Ya'qub, to grant me my request, for my desire is toward You. Glory be to the Creator of light. O Allah, by Your mercy forgive my sins and do not distance me from Your mercy because of my humiliation. Glory be to the Creator of light. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a supplication that is not answered, a prayer that is not accepted, a sin that is not forgiven, and an excuse that is not accepted. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, I seek refuge in the light of Your noble face from my sins that have destroyed me. Glory be to the Creator of light. I have fled to You with my sins and I confess my sin, so do not make me among those who despair, and do not disgrace me on the Day of Judgment. Glory be to the Creator of light. My God, my forehead has been wounded, my tears have dried up, worms have scattered from my knees, and my sin clings to my skin. Glory be to the Creator of light."

He said: Then a call came to him: "O Dawud, are you hungry so that you may be fed? Are you thirsty so that you may be given drink? Are you wronged so that you may be helped?"

He did not answer about the mention of his sin with anything. Then he cried out a cry that stirred all around him, then called: "O Lord, the sin, the sin that I committed!"

He was called: "O Dawud, lift up your head, for I have forgiven you."

He did not lift his head until Jibril (peace be upon him) came and lifted it.

Wahb said: A call came to Dawud (peace be upon him): "I have forgiven you."

He said: "O Lord, how, when You do not wrong anyone?"

He said: "Go to the grave of Uriyah, call out to him, and I will let him hear your call, and seek his pardon."

He went until he came to his grave, wearing a coarse woolen garment, and sat by his grave, then called: "O Uriyah!"

He said: "At your service. Who is this who has interrupted my pleasure and awakened me?"

He said: "I am Dawud."

He said: "What has brought you, O Prophet of Allah?"

He said: "I ask you to make me free of what I did to you!" He said: "And what did you do to me?"

He said: "I exposed you to death."

He said: "You exposed me to Paradise, and you are free of it."

Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed to him: "O Dawud, do you not know that I am a just judge who does not judge by harshness or deception? Did you not inform him that you had married his wife?"

He returned to him, called him, and he answered.

He said: "Who is this who has interrupted my pleasure?"

He said: "I am Dawud."

He said: "O Prophet of Allah, have I not pardoned you?"

He said: "Yes, but I only did that to you because of your wife, and I married her."

He was silent and did not answer him. He called him and he did not answer. He repeated it and he did not answer. Then he stood at his grave and put dust on his head, then called: "Woe to Dawud, then a long woe to him on the day he is seized by the neck and delivered to the wronged one. Glory be to the Creator of light. Woe to Dawud, then a long woe to him on the day he is dragged on his face with the sinners to the Fire. Glory be to the Creator of light. Woe to Dawud, then a long woe to him on the day the guards of Hell bring him near with the wrongdoers to the Fire. Glory be to the Creator of light."

He said: Then a call came to him from the sky: "O Dawud, I have forgiven your sin, had mercy on your weeping, answered your supplication, and removed your stumble."

He said: "O Lord, how can You pardon me when my companion has not pardoned me?"

He said: "O Dawud, I will give him on the Day of Resurrection what no eye has seen and no ear has heard. Then I will say to him: 'Are you pleased with My servant?' He will say: 'O Lord, from where is this for me, when my deed has not reached it?' I will say to him: 'This is in exchange for My servant Dawud, and I will ask you to grant him to Me, and you will grant him to Me.'"

He said: "O Lord, now I know that You have forgiven me."

This is His statement, glorified is He: ﴿So he sought forgiveness from his Lord and fell down bowing and turned in repentance. So We forgave him that﴾, meaning that sin. ﴿And indeed he has, with Us, after forgiveness, nearness and a good place of return﴾, meaning a good return.

It was also related to me by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Makhlad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyya told us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, saying: Abu al-Ilyas, Muqatil, and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jundi informed us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When Allah, mighty and majestic, accepted Dawud's repentance, he wept over his sin for thirty years. A tear did not dry up from him by night or by day. He had committed the sin at the age of seventy. After the sin, he divided time into four days: one day for judging among the Children of Israel, one day for his wives, one day when he traveled in the deserts, the mountains, and the seashore, and one day when he secluded himself in a house of his that contained four thousand prayer niches. The monks would gather to him, and he would lament with them over himself, and they would help him in that. When it was the day of his wandering, he would go out into the deserts and raise his voice with the psalms (al-mazamir), and he would weep, and the trees, the sands, the birds, and the wild beasts would weep with him, until streams of their tears flowed like rivers. Then he would come to the mountains and raise his voice with the psalms, and he would weep, and the stones, the mountains, the animals, and the birds would weep with him, until valleys flowed from their weeping. Then he would come to the seashore and raise his voice with the psalms, and he would weep, and the whales, the creatures of the sea, the beasts, and the water birds would weep with him. When it grew dark, he would return.

When it was the day of his lamentation over himself, his herald would call out: "Today is the day of Dawud lamenting over himself, so let whoever will help him come."

He said: So he would enter the house that contained the prayer niches, and three layers of coarse woolen mats, stuffed with palm fiber, would be spread for him, and he would sit on them. Four thousand monks would come, wearing hooded cloaks and holding staves, and they would sit in those prayer niches. Then Dawud would raise his voice in weeping and lamentation over himself, and the monks would raise their voices with him. He would not cease weeping until the mats were drenched with his tears, and Dawud would fall upon them like a fledgling trembling. Then his son Sulayman would come and lift him up. Dawud would take from those tears with his palms, then wipe his face with them, and say: "O Lord, forgive what You see." If the weeping of Dawud were weighed against the weeping of the people of this world, it would outweigh it.

It was also related to me by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ibn Majah told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ayyub told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad told us, saying: Sayyar told us, from Ja'far, who said: I heard Thabit say: Dawud did not drink any drink after his forgiveness except that it was mixed with the tears of his eyes.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 38, verses 22–28 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Abi al-Atikah narrated to us that among the supplications of David was: "Glory be to You, my God. When I remember my sin, the earth becomes too narrow for me despite its vastness, and when I remember Your mercy, my soul returns to me. My God, I have come to the physicians of Your servants so that they might treat my sin for me, but they all point me toward You" [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/304; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/186.]].
