He said: So there was made for him a throne of elephant tusks, inlaid with rubies, pearls, chrysolite, and various kinds of jewels, and surrounded by four palm trees of gold, whose clusters were of red ruby and green emerald. On the top of two of the palm trees were two golden peacocks, and on the top of the other two were two golden eagles, facing one another. On both sides of the throne were two golden lions, on the top of each of which was a pillar of green emerald. Vines of red gold were woven over the palm trees, and their clusters were of red ruby, such that the arbor of vines shaded the palm trees and the throne.

He said: When Solomon wished to ascend it, he placed his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne turned with what was on it, like a swiftly spinning millstone. The eagles and peacocks spread their wings, and the two lions stretched out their paws and struck the ground with their tails. This was done at every step that Solomon ascended. When he settled at the top, the two eagles on the palm trees took Solomon's crown and placed it on his head. Then the throne turned with what was on it, and the eagles, peacocks, and lions turned with it, their heads inclined toward Solomon, and they sprinkled upon him musk and ambergris from their bellies. Then a golden dove standing on a pillar of jewel, one of the pillars of the throne, took the Torah, and Solomon opened it and read it to the people and called them to a decisive judgment. The nobles of the Children of Israel sat on golden inlaid chairs—there were a thousand chairs—on his right, and the great ones of the jinn came and sat on silver chairs on his left—there were a thousand chairs—all surrounding him. Then the birds encircled them, shading them. The people came forward to him for judgment. When the clear proofs were called for and the witnesses came forward to give testimony, the throne turned with all that was around it, like a swiftly spinning millstone. The two lions stretched out their paws and struck the ground with their tails, and the two eagles and two peacocks spread their wings. The witnesses were terrified by it, and great fear entered them, so they bore witness only to the truth. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/202.]]

﴿He said: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾ (38:35)

Ibn Kaysan said: That is, it will not belong to anyone.

﴿after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾ — "al-Wahhab" means the Giver.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: He means: "Grant me a kingdom that I will not be stripped of for the rest of my life, as I was stripped of it in the past of my life."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Solomon was a king, but by his words ﴿that will not befit anyone after me﴾ he meant the subjugation of the winds and the birds, as indicated by what follows it.

It is also said: He asked for that so that it would be a sign of his prophethood, a proof of his messengership, and a miracle for those other than him.

It is also said: He asked for that so that it would be a sign to him of forgiveness and the acceptance of repentance, since Allah, glorified and exalted, answered his supplication, returned his kingdom to him, and increased it.

'Umar ibn 'Uthman al-Sadafi said: He meant by it the dominion over the self and the subjugation of desire.

This is supported by what:
'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Ifriqi narrated to us, saying: Salman ibn 'Amir al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Have you seen Solomon and what Allah gave him of kingship? He never raised his gaze to the sky in humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until Allah took him." [118] [[Al-Musannaf li Ibn Abi Shayba: 8/118.]]

And Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubada narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us from al-Hasan that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A devil appeared to me last night in my prayer place, like this dog of yours. I seized him and wanted to tie him up until morning, but I remembered the supplication of my brother Solomon: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me,﴾ so I let him go." [119] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/313.]]

And from him, from Rawh, from Shu'ba, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Last night a powerful jinn kept coming at me to cut off my prayer, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, enabled me to overcome him. [In the manuscript: 'fa-rra'ahu'; in the sources: 'fa-akhadhtahu,' 'fa-dha'tahu,' and 'fa-intahartuhu.'] I almost wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque until morning, so that you would all look at him. Then I remembered the words of Solomon: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me,﴾ so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him back defeated." [120] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/298; Sahih al-Bukhari: 4/136.]]

﴿So We subjected to him the wind, flowing gently by his command, wherever he willed.﴾ (38:36)

"Rukhaa'" means gentle and soft. "Haythu asaba" means wherever he intended and willed, in the language of Himyar.

The Arabs say: "asaba al-sawab wa akhta'a al-jawab," meaning he intended the correct answer.

The poet said:
"He hit upon the speech but could not (sustain it),
so he erred in the answer at the critical point." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/205; Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 5/69.]]

﴿And the devils﴾, that is, We subjected to him the devils: ﴿every builder and diver﴾, who extract pearls for him from the sea. He was the first to extract pearls from the sea. ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, meaning bound in chains—its singular is "sifd." ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold, without account.﴾ (38:39)

"Fa-mnun" means: give, from the words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿and do not give (favor) seeking to gain more﴾ (74:6).

The Arabs say: "manna 'alayya bi-raghif," meaning he gave me a loaf of bread.

Al-Hasan said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has never given anyone a gift without making an accounting in it, except Solomon, for Allah, glorified is He, gave him a pleasant gift, and he said: ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow﴾.

﴿or withhold, without account﴾ — he said: if he gives, he will be rewarded, and if he does not give, there will be no blame upon him.

Muqatil said: It concerns the matter of the devils: take whomever you wish of them into your bonds; there is no blame upon you for what you undertake.

﴿Indeed, for him with Us is a near station and a good final return.﴾ (38:40)

"Zulfa" means nearness, and "husn ma'ab" means a good place of return.

﴿And remember Our servant Job.﴾ (38:41)

Muqatil said: His kunya was Abu 'Abd Allah.

﴿When he called to his Lord: "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."﴾ (38:41) — that is, with fatigue, difficulty, affliction, and harm.

Muqatil said: "Hardship" refers to the body, and "torment" refers to his wealth.

There are four readings of "nusb": "nusub" with two dammas, which is the reading of Abu Ja'far; "nasab" with a fatha on the nun and the sad, which is the reading of Ya'qub; "nasb" with a fatha on the nun and a sukun on the sad, which is the transmission of Hubayra from Hafs from 'Asim; and "nasb" with a damma on the nun and a sukun on the sad, which is the reading of the rest.

They differed about the cause of Job's trial:
Wahb said: A man sought Job's help against an injustice he wanted to ward off, but he did not help him, and so he was tested.

Hayyan narrated from al-Kalbi that Job used to fight a king who was an unbeliever, and Job's livestock were in that king's territory. He flattered the king and did not fight him, so he was tested.

Others said: Job had abundant wealth, and he was impressed by his wealth, so he was tested.

﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and drink.﴾ (38:42) — "irkud" means push and move, and "hadha mughtasal" means this is a place to wash.

Then We sent forth for him another cool spring, and he said: "This is cool and a drink."

﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.﴾ (38:43)

﴿And take in your hand a bundle of grass (dighth), and strike with it and do not break your oath.﴾ (38:44) — "dighth" means a bundle of grass.

﴿Indeed, We found him patient. An excellent servant; indeed, he was one who turned back (to Allah) often.﴾ (38:44)

This is the reading of the common people (al-'amma). Abu Ja'far and 'Asim, in the transmission of al-A'sha and al-Tarjumani, read (liyadabbaru) with a single open ya' and no doubling, as an elision.

Al-Hasan said: "Tadabbur of its verses means following them."

﴿And to Dawud We gave Sulayman; an excellent servant, indeed he was ever turning (to Allah). When there were displayed before him, at the time of evening, the swift-footed steeds, ... ﴾ — the people of understanding might be mindful.

Al-Kalbi said: Sulayman (peace be upon him) raided the people of Damascus and Nasibin and took from them a thousand horses.

Muqatil said: Sulayman inherited from his father Dawud a thousand horses, and his father had taken them from the Amalekites.

'Awf related from al-Hasan: "It has reached me that they were horses that came out of the sea, having wings."

They said: Sulayman prayed the first prayer and sat on his throne while the horses were displayed before him. Nine hundred of them were shown to him, and he became aware of the 'Asr prayer when the sun had already set; he had missed the prayer and had not known of it because of the trial that had come upon him, and he was grieved by this, so he said: ﴿Bring them back to me.﴾

So they brought them back to him, and he hamstrung them and struck their necks with the sword, slaughtering them for Allah the Exalted. One hundred horses remained, and what is among people today of horses is from the offspring of those hundred.

Al-Hasan said: When he hamstrung the horses, Allah replaced them for him with something better than them and swifter than the wind, ﴿which ran at his command wherever he willed﴾. He would set out in the morning from Iliya, take his midday rest at Qarir al-Ard in Istakhr, and return in the evening from Qarir [in Kabul]. [Istakhr: one of the oldest cities of Persia and the first seat of its kings, near Yazd (Mu'jam al-Buldan).] [Tafsir al-Tabari 22/85; and in al-Durr al-Manthur 5/227: Sulayman would ride the wind from Istakhr, have his lunch in Bayt al-Maqdis, then return and have his dinner in Istakhr.]

Ibn 'Abbas said: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib about this verse, and he said: "What has reached you about this, O Ibn 'Abbas?"

I said: I heard Ka'b al-Ahbar say: "Sulayman was occupied one day with reviewing the mares and looking at them, until the sun was hidden behind the veil."

When he missed the prayer, he said: ﴿Indeed I have loved the love of good (wealth) over the remembrance of my Lord until (the sun) was hidden behind the veil.﴾ — meaning the mares, which were twenty-four; and it is said fourteen. So they were brought back to him, and he ordered their shanks and necks to be struck with the sword, and he killed them. And Allah stripped him of his kingdom for fourteen days, because he had wronged the horses by killing them.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Ka'b al-Ahbar has lied. Rather, Sulayman was occupied one day with reviewing the horses because he intended to fight an enemy, until the sun was hidden behind the veil, and then he said, by the command of Allah, to the angels assigned to the sun: ﴿Bring it back to me.﴾ — meaning the sun — so they brought it back to him until he prayed the 'Asr in its time."

The prophets of Allah do not wrong, nor do they command wrong, nor do they approve of wrong, for they are protected and purified. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿When there were displayed before him at the time of evening the swift-footed steeds﴾ — al-safinat being the horses standing on three legs, having raised the other on the tip of its hoof, whether a foreleg or a hind leg.

'Amr ibn Kulthum said: "We left the horses cleaving to him, their bridles fastened, standing in ṣuffūn (stillness)."

Al-Qutaybi said: "In the speech of the Arabs, al-safin is the one standing among horses and others."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is pleased that men should stand for him (ṣuffūnan) let him take his seat in the Fire."

[Zad al-Masir 6/334.] [115] That is, standing. ﴿Al-jiyad﴾ — the choice, swift ones, singular jawad.

﴿Indeed I have loved the love of good﴾ — meaning the horses. The Arabs interchange the letters r and l, saying inhamalat al-'ayn and inhamarat, and khatalat al-rajul and khatarahu, meaning he deceived him.

Muqatil said: ﴿love of good﴾ means wealth, and it is the horses that were displayed to him. ﴿From the remembrance of my Lord﴾ means the prayer; a parallel is His words: ﴿Neither trade nor commerce distracts them from the remembrance of Allah﴾ [Surat al-Nur: 37]. ﴿Until (it) was hidden﴾ means the sun, a reference without prior mention, as in the verse of Labid:

"Until, when she cast forth her hand into the disbeliever..." [al-Sihah lil-Jawhari 2/808; the second half of the line is: "and she concealed the darkness of the frontier passes."]

It means the sun ﴿behind the veil﴾, which is a mountain beyond Qaf at a distance of a year's journey, behind which the sun sets.

﴿Bring them back to me﴾ — return them to me. ﴿So he began to pass his hand over their shanks and necks﴾ — meaning he set about passing the sword over their shanks and necks, and slaughtering them, drawing near to Allah the Exalted by them and seeking His pleasure, since they had occupied him from His obedience. That was a sacrifice from him and permitted to him, just as the slaughter of livestock cattle is permitted to us.

Some said: the meaning is that he confined them in the path of Allah, and branded their shanks and necks with a mark like the mark of charity (sadaqah).

The brand on the shank is called 'ilaz, and the brand on the neck is called dahaw.

Al-Zuhri and Ibn Kaysan said: He would pass his hand over their shanks and necks, and wipe the dust from them, out of love for them.

This is the transmission of Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas.

﴿And indeed We tried Sulayman﴾ — this is the story of the trial of the prophet of Allah Sulayman and the cause of the temporary loss of his kingdom, and they differed about the cause of that.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from some scholars, who said: Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Sulayman heard of a city on an island among the islands of the sea called Saydun, which had a great king, and no one could reach him because of his place in the sea. Allah had given Sulayman in his kingdom an authority such that nothing was withheld from him on land or sea; he would ride to it [when he rode] on the wind. He set out to that city, carried by the wind over the surface of the water, until he descended there with his armies of jinn and men. He killed its king and settled there, and among what he obtained was a daughter of that king called Jaradah, whose beauty and loveliness no one had seen the like of. He chose her for himself and invited her to Islam, and she embraced Islam with some reluctance and little trust. He loved her with a love he had not felt for any of his other wives. She kept her standing with him, but her sorrow did not depart and her tears did not dry. This grieved Sulayman, and he said to her: "Woe to you, what is this sorrow that does not leave and this tearfulness that does not dry?"

She said: "My father occupies my mind; I remember him and his kingdom and what he had and what befell him, and that saddens me."

Sulayman said: "Allah has given you in exchange a kingdom greater than his, and an authority greater than his authority, and guided you to Islam, which is better than all that."

She said: "That is indeed so, but when I remember him the sorrow I see afflicts me. If only you would command the devils to fashion his image in my house, where I am, so that I might see it morning and evening, I would hope that this would remove my sorrow and console me for some of what I feel within myself."

So Sulayman commanded the devils and said: "Make for her an image of her father in her house, so that she does not fail to recognize anything of him."

They fashioned it for her until she looked upon her father with his very eyes, except that there was no spirit in it. She then took it from the moment they made it, dressed it in an izar, a shirt and a turban, and clothed it in the garments he used to wear. Then whenever Sulayman left her house, she would go out in the morning among her maidservants to prostrate to it, and they would prostrate with her, as she used to do to him in his kingdom; and she would do the same each evening. Sulayman did not know anything of this for forty mornings. This reached Asaf ibn Barkhiya, who was a truthful man (siddiq), and who was never turned away from Sulayman's door at any hour when he wished to enter any of his houses, whether Sulayman was present or absent. He came to him and said: "O prophet of Allah, my years have grown great, my bones have grown weak, my life has run out, and the time of my departure has come. I wish to stand one station before death, in which I may mention those prophets of Allah who have passed, and praise them according to my knowledge of them, and inform people of some of what they were ignorant of concerning many of their affairs."

He said: "Do it."

So Sulayman gathered the people for him, and he stood among them preaching, mentioning those prophets of Allah who had passed, praising each prophet for what was in him and mentioning what Allah had favoured him with, until he came to Sulayman and said: "How forbearing you were in your youth, how scrupulous in your youth, how excellent in your youth, how sound your affairs were in your youth, how far you were in your youth from everything disliked," and then he departed.

Sulayman felt something in himself about this until it filled him with anger. When Sulayman entered his house, he sent for him and said:

"O Asaf, you mentioned those prophets of Allah who had passed and praised them well in every age and in every state of their affairs. Yet when you mentioned me, you praised me well in my youth and kept silent about everything else of my affairs in my old age. What have you done in the last part of my life?"

He said: "Indeed, other than Allah has been worshipped in your house these forty mornings, for the sake of a woman's desire."

He said: "In my house?"

He said: "In your house."

He said: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return. I know well that you said what you said only because of something that reached you."

Then Sulayman returned to his house and broke that idol, and punished that woman and her maidservants. Then he commanded the garments of purity to be brought—and they are garments that only virgins spin, and which no woman who has seen blood has touched—and he put them on, then went out alone into a barren land and commanded ashes to be spread for him. Then he came back repenting to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until he sat upon those ashes and rolled in them in his garments, humbling himself before Allah the Exalted and beseeching Him, weeping, calling upon Him and asking forgiveness for what had happened in his house, and saying in what he said: "My Lord, what is Your tribulation for the family of Dawud, that they should worship other than You, and that they should remain in their houses and families in worship of other than You?"

He remained so that day until evening, then returned to his house. He had an umm walad called al-Aminah. Whenever he entered the place of relieving himself, or wished to approach one of his women, he would place his ring with her until he had purified himself, and he would not wear his ring except in a state of purity, and his kingdom was in his ring. One day he placed it with her as he usually did, then entered the privy. The devil of the sea came to her, and his name was Sakhr, in the form of Sulayman, so that she would not notice anything of him.

He said: "O Aminah, my ring!"

She handed it to him, and he put it on his hand, then went out and sat on Sulayman's throne, and the birds, the jinn and the men gathered around him. Sulayman came out and went to al-Aminah, and his state and awe had changed in the eyes of everyone who saw him. He said: "O Aminah, my ring!"

She said: "Who are you?"

He said: "I am Sulayman ibn Dawud."

She said: "You lie. You are not Sulayman, for Sulayman has come and taken his ring, and he is sitting on his throne in his kingdom."

Sulayman knew that his sin had overtaken him. He went out and began to stand at the houses of the Children of Israel, saying: "I am Sulayman ibn Dawud." They threw dust on him, abused him, and said: "Look at this madman, what is he saying? He claims to be Sulayman ibn Dawud!"

When Sulayman saw this, he went to the sea and began carrying fish for the fishermen to the market, and they would give him two fish each day. When evening came he would sell one of his two fish for loaves of bread and roast the other, and eat it. He remained thus for forty mornings, the same number of days that man had worshipped that idol in his house. Asaf and the notables of the Children of Israel disapproved of the judgement of the enemy of Allah, the devil, during those forty days.

Asaf said: "O assembly of the Children of Israel, have you seen a change in the judgement of the son of Dawud like what I have seen?"

They said: "Yes."

He said: "Give me time until I enter upon his wives and ask them whether they noticed in his private affairs what we noticed in his public affairs and openly." So he entered upon his wives and said: "Woe to you, did you notice in the affairs of the son of Dawud what we noticed?"

They said: "Worse than that: he does not leave a woman of ours in her blood, nor does he perform ghusl from janabah."

He said: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return... Indeed this is manifest trial."

Then he went out to the Children of Israel and said: "What is in private is no greater than what is in public." When forty mornings had passed, the devil flew away from his seat, then passed by the sea and threw the ring into it. A fish swallowed it, and some of the fishermen caught it. Sulayman had worked that whole day, and when evening came he gave him his fish, and gave him the fish that had taken the ring. Sulayman went out with his two fish, and sold the one with no ring in its belly for loaves of bread. Then he set about slitting open the other fish to roast it, and his ring met him in its belly. He took it and put it on his hand, and fell down prostrate, and the birds and jinn gathered around him, and people came toward him. He recognized the one who had entered upon him because of what he had done in his house. He returned to his kingdom, manifested repentance for his sin, and commanded the devils, saying: "Bring me Sakhr."

The devils searched for him until they seized him and brought him. A rock came to him, and he put him into it, then closed another over him, and fastened them with lead and iron. Then he commanded him to be cast into the sea.

This is the report of Wahb ibn Munabbih [in full in Tarikh al-Tabari 1/351–354].

Al-Suddi said concerning the cause of that: Sulayman (peace be upon him) had a hundred wives, and one of them was called Jaradah, and she was the most devoted of his wives and the most trusted by him. Whenever he relieved himself or had some need, he would take off his ring, and he entrusted it to no one among the people except her. One day she came to him and said: "My brother has a dispute with so-and-so, and I would love for you to judge in his favour when he comes to you."

He said: "Yes," but he did not do it. He was tested by his word, and he gave her his ring and entered the privy, and the devil came out in his form and said to her: "Give me the ring."

She gave it to him, and he came and sat in Sulayman's place. Sulayman came out after him and asked her to give him his ring.

She said: "Did you not take it before?"

He said: "No," and he went away from his place bewildered. The devil remained judging among the people for forty days.

He said: "The people denounced his judgement. The reciters and scholars of the Children of Israel gathered and came to his wives and said: 'We have denounced this. If this is Sulayman, then his mind has gone, and we denounce his judgements.' The women then wept." He said: "They came walking until they reached him, surrounded him, then opened the Torah and read it. When they read the Torah, it flew from between their hands until it alighted on a battlement, with the ring along with it. Then it flew until it went to the sea, and the ring fell from it into the sea, and a whale swallowed it."

He said: "Sulayman went on in the state he was in, until he came to a fisherman from the fishermen of the sea. He was hungry and his hunger had grown severe, so he asked him for some of their catch and said: 'I am Sulayman.'"

One of them rose to him and struck him with a stick, splitting his head.

He said: "He began washing his blood while on the shore of the sea. The fishermen blamed their companion who had struck him and said: 'What an evil thing you did in striking him.'"

He said: "He said: 'He claims he is Sulayman.' They gave him two fish from among what had already begun to spoil with them. The pain of his beating did not distract him, until he went to the edge of the sea, split open their bellies and began washing them, and found his ring in the belly of one of them. He took it and put it on, and Allah restored to him his kingdom and splendour, and the birds came and hovered over him, so the people knew that he was Sulayman, and they rose making excuses for what they had done."

He said: "I do not praise you for your excuse, nor do I blame you for what happened from you; this was a matter that had to be."

Then he came until he reached his kingdom, and commanded that the devil who had taken his ring be brought. He put him in an iron chest, sealed it, closed it with a lock, stamped it with his ring, and then commanded that it be cast into the sea, where he remains alive until the Hour." [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/38; Tarikh al-Tabari 1/354.]

In some reports: when Sulayman was tried, the ring fell from his hand, and his kingdom was in it. Sulayman took it and returned it to his hand, but it fell from his hand again. When Sulayman saw that it would not stay on his hand, he was certain of the trial, and Asaf said to Sulayman: "You are tried for your sin, and the ring will not hold fast on your hand for fourteen days. Flee to Allah repentant of your sin, and I will stand in your place, go about in your world and your households with your conduct, until Allah accepts your repentance and returns you to your kingdom."

So Sulayman fled, running to his Lord, and Asaf took the ring and placed it on his hand, and it held. And the body of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾ was Asaf, who was a scribe for Sulayman and had knowledge of the Book. Asaf remained in Sulayman's kingdom and world, going about by his conduct and acting by his deeds for fourteen days, until Sulayman returned to his dwelling repentant to Allah the Exalted, and Allah restored his kingdom to him. Asaf then rose from his seat, Sulayman sat on his throne, and he put the ring back on his hand, and it held there.

Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar informed us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that Sulayman ibn Dawud secluded himself from the people for three days, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "O Sulayman, you secluded yourself from the people for three days, and so you did not look into the affairs of My servants, and did not give justice to the oppressed against the oppressor."

He mentioned the hadith of the ring and the devil's seizing it as we have narrated it [in full in Tarikh Dimashq 22/248, ed. Dar al-Fikr].

At its end he said: "'Ali said: I mentioned that to al-Hasan, and he said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not have given him power over his wives.'" [al-Durr al-Manthur 5/312.]

Some exegetes said: The cause of Solomon's trial was that he had been commanded not to marry any woman except from the Children of Israel, but he married a woman from outside them, and he was punished for that.

It is also said: When Solomon took the daughter of the king of Sidon, he was impressed by her, so he invited her to Islam. She refused and resisted, so Solomon threatened her.

She said: "If you force me to embrace Islam, I will kill myself."

Solomon feared she would kill herself, so he married her while she was still a polytheist. For forty days she worshipped an idol of hers made of ruby, secretly from Solomon, until she embraced Islam. Solomon was punished by the loss of his kingdom for forty days.

Al-Sha'bi said regarding the cause: A son was born to Solomon. The devils gathered, and some of them said to others: "If he lives and has a child, we will not be freed from what we are in of affliction and of sorcery. Our way is to kill his child or to harm him."

Solomon learned of this, so he commanded the clouds, and the wind carried his son in the clouds, lest the devil harm him. Allah punished him for his fear of the devil, and the child died. He was cast dead onto his throne, and this is the body that Allah, glorified is He, mentioned: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back (in repentance).﴾ (38:34)

It is also said: Solomon said one day: "Tonight I will go around to all my wives, so that from each one of them a son will be born who will fight in the way of Allah." He did not say "if Allah wills" (in sha' Allah), so he had intercourse with all of them in one night, and none of them bore anything except a half-formed child. The midwife brought it and placed it on Solomon's throne.

This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿a body﴾. This is what was narrated to us by Abdullah ibn Hamid from others, who said: Ibn al-Sharqi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Aqil and Ahmad ibn Hafs narrated to us, both saying: Hafs narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to me from Musa ibn 'Uqba, who said: Abu al-Zinad informed me from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sulayman ibn Dawud said: 'Tonight I will go around to seventy women, each of whom will bring forth a horseman who will fight in the way of Allah.' His companion said to him: 'Say: if Allah wills.' But he did not say: 'if Allah wills.' So he went around to them, and none of them conceived except one woman, who brought forth half a man. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if he had said: 'if Allah wills,' they would all have fought in the way of Allah as horsemen." [116] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/209; Sahih Muslim: 5/87.]]

This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
﴿And We indeed tested Solomon.﴾

Muqatil said: Solomon was tested after he had ruled for twenty years, and he ruled for twenty years after the trial.

﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾, that is, a devil, according to most exegetes.

They differed about his name. Muqatil and Qatada said: His name is Sakhr ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amr ibn Sharahil, and he is the one who showed Solomon the diamond (al-almas) when he commanded that the Temple of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) be built, and it was said to him: "Let no sound of iron be heard in it." So they took the diamond and began to cut the stones and the jewels with it, and no sound was heard. Whenever Solomon wished to enter the privy (al-khala') or the bath, he would not enter with his ring. He entered the bath, and the story is mentioned about the devil's taking of the ring.

He said: Among them there was a man whom they compared with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab in strength. He said: "By Allah, I will test him." So he said: "O Prophet of Allah," while he did not see that he was the Prophet of Allah: "Do you see that if one of us becomes impure from sexual intercourse on a cold night, and he deliberately leaves washing until the sun rises, is there any harm upon him?" He said: "No." So he granted him leave in that, and he mentioned the hadith.

Abu Ishaq narrated from 'Imara ibn 'Abd from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "While Solomon was sitting on the shore of the sea playing with his ring, it fell into the sea, and his kingdom was in his ring."

Hammad ibn Salama narrated from 'Amr ibn Dinar from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The engraving on the ring of Sulayman ibn Dawud was: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." [117] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/498, no. 32337; Tadhkirat al-Mawdu'at: 108.]]

Returning to the hadith of 'Ali, he said: Solomon departed and left a devil in his household, and he came to an old woman and took refuge with her. The old woman said to him: "If you wish to go and seek (work), I will take care of the household work for you; or if you wish, you take care of the house and go and search."

He said: So he went searching. He came upon some people fishing, and he sat with them. They threw him some fish, so he took them and went to the old woman. She began to prepare them, and she split open the belly of a fish, and in it was the ring. She took it and said to Solomon: "What is this?"

Solomon took it and put it on, and the devils, the jinn, humans, birds, and beasts came to him. The devil who had been left in his household fled, and he came to an island in the sea. They sent devils to him, and they said: "We cannot overcome him, but he comes to us on the island once every seven days, one day. We cannot overcome him until he becomes intoxicated."

He said: So they drained its water and put wine in it. He said: When the day of his arrival came, he found the wine, and he said: "By Allah, you are indeed a good drink, except that you affect the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance." Then he left, until he became very thirsty, and then he came to it and said: "Indeed you are a good drink, except that you affect the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance."

He said: Then he drank it until it overcame his mind. Then they showed him the ring, and he said: "I hear and obey." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 22/187.]]

He said: So they brought him to Solomon, who bound him and then sent him to a mountain. It is said that it is the mountain of smoke that they see from him, and the water that comes out of the mountain is his urine.

Al-Suddi said: The name of that devil is Ismadhi, and it was said Khabfiq.

Mujahid said: His name is Asif.

Abu Salih ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Bayhaqi, the jurist, informed us, saying: Abu Hatim al-Tamimi informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar al-'Abdi narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubada narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us from Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid regarding ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾, who said: "A devil called Asif." Solomon said to him: "How do you deceive the people?"

He said: "Show me your ring, and I will tell you." When he gave it to him, he threw it into the sea. Solomon wandered, and his kingdom was lost. Asif sat on his throne, and Allah prevented Solomon's wives from him, so he did not approach them. The people denied Solomon's affair. Solomon used to ask for food and say: "Do you recognize me? I am Solomon," but they would deny him, until one day a woman gave him a fish. He split its belly and found his ring in its belly. His kingdom returned to him, and Asif fled and entered the sea. It was also said: The body is Asif ibn Barkhiya, the truthful, and the story has passed.

It is also said: It is the dead child who was carried off in the clouds.

It is also said: It is the child with a deformed creation.

It is also said: The meaning of His words ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾ is that Solomon was struck by an illness from which he approached death, until he became a body in the proverbial sense, without a soul. The emaciated sick person is described with this description, and it is said: "Like a body cast down," and nothing remained of him except his body. The sense of the verse is: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾.

As for the description of Solomon's throne:
It is narrated that when Solomon became king after his father, he commanded that a throne be made for him to sit on for judgment, and he commanded that it be made wondrous and awe-inspiring, such that if a wrongdoer or a false witness saw it, he would be restrained and awed.

He said: So there was made for him a throne of elephant tusks, inlaid with rubies, pearls, chrysolite, and various kinds of jewels, and surrounded by four palm trees of gold, whose clusters were of red ruby and green emerald. On the top of two of the palm trees were two golden peacocks, and on the top of the other two were two golden eagles, facing one another. On both sides of the throne were two golden lions, on the top of each of which was a pillar of green emerald. Vines of red gold were woven over the palm trees, and their clusters were of red ruby, such that the arbor of vines shaded the palm trees and the throne.

He said: When Solomon wished to ascend it, he placed his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne turned with what was on it, like a swiftly spinning millstone. The eagles and peacocks spread their wings, and the two lions stretched out their paws and struck the ground with their tails. This was done at every step that Solomon ascended. When he settled at the top, the two eagles on the palm trees took Solomon's crown and placed it on his head. Then the throne turned with what was on it, and the eagles, peacocks, and lions turned with it, their heads inclined toward Solomon, and they sprinkled upon him musk and ambergris from their bellies. Then a golden dove standing on a pillar of jewel, one of the pillars of the throne, took the Torah, and Solomon opened it and read it to the people and called them to a decisive judgment. The nobles of the Children of Israel sat on golden inlaid chairs—there were a thousand chairs—on his right, and the great ones of the jinn came and sat on silver chairs on his left—there were a thousand chairs—all surrounding him. Then the birds encircled them, shading them. The people came forward to him for judgment. When the clear proofs were called for and the witnesses came forward to give testimony, the throne turned with all that was around it, like a swiftly spinning millstone. The two lions stretched out their paws and struck the ground with their tails, and the two eagles and two peacocks spread their wings. The witnesses were terrified by it, and great fear entered them, so they bore witness only to the truth. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/202.]]

﴿He said: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾ (38:35)

Ibn Kaysan said: That is, it will not belong to anyone.

﴿after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾ — "al-Wahhab" means the Giver.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: He means: "Grant me a kingdom that I will not be stripped of for the rest of my life, as I was stripped of it in the past of my life."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Solomon was a king, but by his words ﴿that will not befit anyone after me﴾ he meant the subjugation of the winds and the birds, as indicated by what follows it.

It is also said: He asked for that so that it would be a sign of his prophethood, a proof of his messengership, and a miracle for those other than him.

It is also said: He asked for that so that it would be a sign to him of forgiveness and the acceptance of repentance, since Allah, glorified and exalted, answered his supplication, returned his kingdom to him, and increased it.

'Umar ibn 'Uthman al-Sadafi said: He meant by it the dominion over the self and the subjugation of desire.

This is supported by what:
'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Ifriqi narrated to us, saying: Salman ibn 'Amir al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Have you seen Solomon and what Allah gave him of kingship? He never raised his gaze to the sky in humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until Allah took him." [118] [[Al-Musannaf li Ibn Abi Shayba: 8/118.]]

And Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubada narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us from al-Hasan that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A devil appeared to me last night in my prayer place, like this dog of yours. I seized him and wanted to tie him up until morning, but I remembered the supplication of my brother Solomon: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me,﴾ so I let him go." [119] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/313.]]

And from him, from Rawh, from Shu'ba, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Last night a powerful jinn kept coming at me to cut off my prayer, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, enabled me to overcome him. [In the manuscript: 'fa-rra'ahu'; in the sources: 'fa-akhadhtahu,' 'fa-dha'tahu,' and 'fa-intahartuhu.'] I almost wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque until morning, so that you would all look at him. Then I remembered the words of Solomon: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me,﴾ so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him back defeated." [120] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/298; Sahih al-Bukhari: 4/136.]]

﴿So We subjected to him the wind, flowing gently by his command, wherever he willed.﴾ (38:36)

"Rukhaa'" means gentle and soft. "Haythu asaba" means wherever he intended and willed, in the language of Himyar.

The Arabs say: "asaba al-sawab wa akhta'a al-jawab," meaning he intended the correct answer.

The poet said:
"He hit upon the speech but could not (sustain it),
so he erred in the answer at the critical point." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/205; Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 5/69.]]

﴿And the devils﴾, that is, We subjected to him the devils: ﴿every builder and diver﴾, who extract pearls for him from the sea. He was the first to extract pearls from the sea. ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, meaning bound in chains—its singular is "sifd." ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold, without account.﴾ (38:39)

"Fa-mnun" means: give, from the words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿and do not give (favor) seeking to gain more﴾ (74:6).

The Arabs say: "manna 'alayya bi-raghif," meaning he gave me a loaf of bread.

Al-Hasan said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has never given anyone a gift without making an accounting in it, except Solomon, for Allah, glorified is He, gave him a pleasant gift, and he said: ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow﴾.

﴿or withhold, without account﴾ — he said: if he gives, he will be rewarded, and if he does not give, there will be no blame upon him.

Muqatil said: It concerns the matter of the devils: take whomever you wish of them into your bonds; there is no blame upon you for what you undertake.

﴿Indeed, for him with Us is a near station and a good final return.﴾ (38:40)

"Zulfa" means nearness, and "husn ma'ab" means a good place of return.

﴿And remember Our servant Job.﴾ (38:41)

Muqatil said: His kunya was Abu 'Abd Allah.

﴿When he called to his Lord: "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."﴾ (38:41) — that is, with fatigue, difficulty, affliction, and harm.

Muqatil said: "Hardship" refers to the body, and "torment" refers to his wealth.

There are four readings of "nusb": "nusub" with two dammas, which is the reading of Abu Ja'far; "nasab" with a fatha on the nun and the sad, which is the reading of Ya'qub; "nasb" with a fatha on the nun and a sukun on the sad, which is the transmission of Hubayra from Hafs from 'Asim; and "nasb" with a damma on the nun and a sukun on the sad, which is the reading of the rest.

They differed about the cause of Job's trial:
Wahb said: A man sought Job's help against an injustice he wanted to ward off, but he did not help him, and so he was tested.

Hayyan narrated from al-Kalbi that Job used to fight a king who was an unbeliever, and Job's livestock were in that king's territory. He flattered the king and did not fight him, so he was tested.

Others said: Job had abundant wealth, and he was impressed by his wealth, so he was tested.

﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and drink.﴾ (38:42) — "irkud" means push and move, and "hadha mughtasal" means this is a place to wash.

Then We sent forth for him another cool spring, and he said: "This is cool and a drink."

﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.﴾ (38:43)

﴿And take in your hand a bundle of grass (dighth), and strike with it and do not break your oath.﴾ (38:44) — "dighth" means a bundle of grass.

﴿Indeed, We found him patient. An excellent servant; indeed, he was one who turned back (to Allah) often.﴾ (38:44)

This is the reading of the common people (al-'amma). Abu Ja'far and 'Asim, in the transmission of al-A'sha and al-Tarjumani, read (liyadabbaru) with a single open ya' and no doubling, as an elision.

Al-Hasan said: "Tadabbur of its verses means following them."

﴿And to Dawud We gave Sulayman; an excellent servant, indeed he was ever turning (to Allah). When there were displayed before him, at the time of evening, the swift-footed steeds, ... ﴾ — the people of understanding might be mindful.

Al-Kalbi said: Sulayman (peace be upon him) raided the people of Damascus and Nasibin and took from them a thousand horses.

Muqatil said: Sulayman inherited from his father Dawud a thousand horses, and his father had taken them from the Amalekites.

'Awf related from al-Hasan: "It has reached me that they were horses that came out of the sea, having wings."

They said: Sulayman prayed the first prayer and sat on his throne while the horses were displayed before him. Nine hundred of them were shown to him, and he became aware of the 'Asr prayer when the sun had already set; he had missed the prayer and had not known of it because of the trial that had come upon him, and he was grieved by this, so he said: ﴿Bring them back to me.﴾

So they brought them back to him, and he hamstrung them and struck their necks with the sword, slaughtering them for Allah the Exalted. One hundred horses remained, and what is among people today of horses is from the offspring of those hundred.

Al-Hasan said: When he hamstrung the horses, Allah replaced them for him with something better than them and swifter than the wind, ﴿which ran at his command wherever he willed﴾. He would set out in the morning from Iliya, take his midday rest at Qarir al-Ard in Istakhr, and return in the evening from Qarir [in Kabul]. [Istakhr: one of the oldest cities of Persia and the first seat of its kings, near Yazd (Mu'jam al-Buldan).] [Tafsir al-Tabari 22/85; and in al-Durr al-Manthur 5/227: Sulayman would ride the wind from Istakhr, have his lunch in Bayt al-Maqdis, then return and have his dinner in Istakhr.]

Ibn 'Abbas said: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib about this verse, and he said: "What has reached you about this, O Ibn 'Abbas?"

I said: I heard Ka'b al-Ahbar say: "Sulayman was occupied one day with reviewing the mares and looking at them, until the sun was hidden behind the veil."

When he missed the prayer, he said: ﴿Indeed I have loved the love of good (wealth) over the remembrance of my Lord until (the sun) was hidden behind the veil.﴾ — meaning the mares, which were twenty-four; and it is said fourteen. So they were brought back to him, and he ordered their shanks and necks to be struck with the sword, and he killed them. And Allah stripped him of his kingdom for fourteen days, because he had wronged the horses by killing them.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Ka'b al-Ahbar has lied. Rather, Sulayman was occupied one day with reviewing the horses because he intended to fight an enemy, until the sun was hidden behind the veil, and then he said, by the command of Allah, to the angels assigned to the sun: ﴿Bring it back to me.﴾ — meaning the sun — so they brought it back to him until he prayed the 'Asr in its time."

The prophets of Allah do not wrong, nor do they command wrong, nor do they approve of wrong, for they are protected and purified. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿When there were displayed before him at the time of evening the swift-footed steeds﴾ — al-safinat being the horses standing on three legs, having raised the other on the tip of its hoof, whether a foreleg or a hind leg.

'Amr ibn Kulthum said: "We left the horses cleaving to him, their bridles fastened, standing in ṣuffūn (stillness)."

Al-Qutaybi said: "In the speech of the Arabs, al-safin is the one standing among horses and others."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is pleased that men should stand for him (ṣuffūnan) let him take his seat in the Fire."

[Zad al-Masir 6/334.] [115] That is, standing. ﴿Al-jiyad﴾ — the choice, swift ones, singular jawad.

﴿Indeed I have loved the love of good﴾ — meaning the horses. The Arabs interchange the letters r and l, saying inhamalat al-'ayn and inhamarat, and khatalat al-rajul and khatarahu, meaning he deceived him.

Muqatil said: ﴿love of good﴾ means wealth, and it is the horses that were displayed to him. ﴿From the remembrance of my Lord﴾ means the prayer; a parallel is His words: ﴿Neither trade nor commerce distracts them from the remembrance of Allah﴾ [Surat al-Nur: 37]. ﴿Until (it) was hidden﴾ means the sun, a reference without prior mention, as in the verse of Labid:

"Until, when she cast forth her hand into the disbeliever..." [al-Sihah lil-Jawhari 2/808; the second half of the line is: "and she concealed the darkness of the frontier passes."]

It means the sun ﴿behind the veil﴾, which is a mountain beyond Qaf at a distance of a year's journey, behind which the sun sets.

﴿Bring them back to me﴾ — return them to me. ﴿So he began to pass his hand over their shanks and necks﴾ — meaning he set about passing the sword over their shanks and necks, and slaughtering them, drawing near to Allah the Exalted by them and seeking His pleasure, since they had occupied him from His obedience. That was a sacrifice from him and permitted to him, just as the slaughter of livestock cattle is permitted to us.

Some said: the meaning is that he confined them in the path of Allah, and branded their shanks and necks with a mark like the mark of charity (sadaqah).

The brand on the shank is called 'ilaz, and the brand on the neck is called dahaw.

Al-Zuhri and Ibn Kaysan said: He would pass his hand over their shanks and necks, and wipe the dust from them, out of love for them.

This is the transmission of Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas.

﴿And indeed We tried Sulayman﴾ — this is the story of the trial of the prophet of Allah Sulayman and the cause of the temporary loss of his kingdom, and they differed about the cause of that.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from some scholars, who said: Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Sulayman heard of a city on an island among the islands of the sea called Saydun, which had a great king, and no one could reach him because of his place in the sea. Allah had given Sulayman in his kingdom an authority such that nothing was withheld from him on land or sea; he would ride to it [when he rode] on the wind. He set out to that city, carried by the wind over the surface of the water, until he descended there with his armies of jinn and men. He killed its king and settled there, and among what he obtained was a daughter of that king called Jaradah, whose beauty and loveliness no one had seen the like of. He chose her for himself and invited her to Islam, and she embraced Islam with some reluctance and little trust. He loved her with a love he had not felt for any of his other wives. She kept her standing with him, but her sorrow did not depart and her tears did not dry. This grieved Sulayman, and he said to her: "Woe to you, what is this sorrow that does not leave and this tearfulness that does not dry?"

She said: "My father occupies my mind; I remember him and his kingdom and what he had and what befell him, and that saddens me."

Sulayman said: "Allah has given you in exchange a kingdom greater than his, and an authority greater than his authority, and guided you to Islam, which is better than all that."

She said: "That is indeed so, but when I remember him the sorrow I see afflicts me. If only you would command the devils to fashion his image in my house, where I am, so that I might see it morning and evening, I would hope that this would remove my sorrow and console me for some of what I feel within myself."

So Sulayman commanded the devils and said: "Make for her an image of her father in her house, so that she does not fail to recognize anything of him."

They fashioned it for her until she looked upon her father with his very eyes, except that there was no spirit in it. She then took it from the moment they made it, dressed it in an izar, a shirt and a turban, and clothed it in the garments he used to wear. Then whenever Sulayman left her house, she would go out in the morning among her maidservants to prostrate to it, and they would prostrate with her, as she used to do to him in his kingdom; and she would do the same each evening. Sulayman did not know anything of this for forty mornings. This reached Asaf ibn Barkhiya, who was a truthful man (siddiq), and who was never turned away from Sulayman's door at any hour when he wished to enter any of his houses, whether Sulayman was present or absent. He came to him and said: "O prophet of Allah, my years have grown great, my bones have grown weak, my life has run out, and the time of my departure has come. I wish to stand one station before death, in which I may mention those prophets of Allah who have passed, and praise them according to my knowledge of them, and inform people of some of what they were ignorant of concerning many of their affairs."

He said: "Do it."

So Sulayman gathered the people for him, and he stood among them preaching, mentioning those prophets of Allah who had passed, praising each prophet for what was in him and mentioning what Allah had favoured him with, until he came to Sulayman and said: "How forbearing you were in your youth, how scrupulous in your youth, how excellent in your youth, how sound your affairs were in your youth, how far you were in your youth from everything disliked," and then he departed.

Sulayman felt something in himself about this until it filled him with anger. When Sulayman entered his house, he sent for him and said:

"O Asaf, you mentioned those prophets of Allah who had passed and praised them well in every age and in every state of their affairs. Yet when you mentioned me, you praised me well in my youth and kept silent about everything else of my affairs in my old age. What have you done in the last part of my life?"

He said: "Indeed, other than Allah has been worshipped in your house these forty mornings, for the sake of a woman's desire."

He said: "In my house?"

He said: "In your house."

He said: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return. I know well that you said what you said only because of something that reached you."

Then Sulayman returned to his house and broke that idol, and punished that woman and her maidservants. Then he commanded the garments of purity to be brought—and they are garments that only virgins spin, and which no woman who has seen blood has touched—and he put them on, then went out alone into a barren land and commanded ashes to be spread for him. Then he came back repenting to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until he sat upon those ashes and rolled in them in his garments, humbling himself before Allah the Exalted and beseeching Him, weeping, calling upon Him and asking forgiveness for what had happened in his house, and saying in what he said: "My Lord, what is Your tribulation for the family of Dawud, that they should worship other than You, and that they should remain in their houses and families in worship of other than You?"

He remained so that day until evening, then returned to his house. He had an umm walad called al-Aminah. Whenever he entered the place of relieving himself, or wished to approach one of his women, he would place his ring with her until he had purified himself, and he would not wear his ring except in a state of purity, and his kingdom was in his ring. One day he placed it with her as he usually did, then entered the privy. The devil of the sea came to her, and his name was Sakhr, in the form of Sulayman, so that she would not notice anything of him.

He said: "O Aminah, my ring!"

She handed it to him, and he put it on his hand, then went out and sat on Sulayman's throne, and the birds, the jinn and the men gathered around him. Sulayman came out and went to al-Aminah, and his state and awe had changed in the eyes of everyone who saw him. He said: "O Aminah, my ring!"

She said: "Who are you?"

He said: "I am Sulayman ibn Dawud."

She said: "You lie. You are not Sulayman, for Sulayman has come and taken his ring, and he is sitting on his throne in his kingdom."

Sulayman knew that his sin had overtaken him. He went out and began to stand at the houses of the Children of Israel, saying: "I am Sulayman ibn Dawud." They threw dust on him, abused him, and said: "Look at this madman, what is he saying? He claims to be Sulayman ibn Dawud!"

When Sulayman saw this, he went to the sea and began carrying fish for the fishermen to the market, and they would give him two fish each day. When evening came he would sell one of his two fish for loaves of bread and roast the other, and eat it. He remained thus for forty mornings, the same number of days that man had worshipped that idol in his house. Asaf and the notables of the Children of Israel disapproved of the judgement of the enemy of Allah, the devil, during those forty days.

Asaf said: "O assembly of the Children of Israel, have you seen a change in the judgement of the son of Dawud like what I have seen?"

They said: "Yes."

He said: "Give me time until I enter upon his wives and ask them whether they noticed in his private affairs what we noticed in his public affairs and openly." So he entered upon his wives and said: "Woe to you, did you notice in the affairs of the son of Dawud what we noticed?"

They said: "Worse than that: he does not leave a woman of ours in her blood, nor does he perform ghusl from janabah."

He said: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return... Indeed this is manifest trial."

Then he went out to the Children of Israel and said: "What is in private is no greater than what is in public." When forty mornings had passed, the devil flew away from his seat, then passed by the sea and threw the ring into it. A fish swallowed it, and some of the fishermen caught it. Sulayman had worked that whole day, and when evening came he gave him his fish, and gave him the fish that had taken the ring. Sulayman went out with his two fish, and sold the one with no ring in its belly for loaves of bread. Then he set about slitting open the other fish to roast it, and his ring met him in its belly. He took it and put it on his hand, and fell down prostrate, and the birds and jinn gathered around him, and people came toward him. He recognized the one who had entered upon him because of what he had done in his house. He returned to his kingdom, manifested repentance for his sin, and commanded the devils, saying: "Bring me Sakhr."

The devils searched for him until they seized him and brought him. A rock came to him, and he put him into it, then closed another over him, and fastened them with lead and iron. Then he commanded him to be cast into the sea.

This is the report of Wahb ibn Munabbih [in full in Tarikh al-Tabari 1/351–354].

Al-Suddi said concerning the cause of that: Sulayman (peace be upon him) had a hundred wives, and one of them was called Jaradah, and she was the most devoted of his wives and the most trusted by him. Whenever he relieved himself or had some need, he would take off his ring, and he entrusted it to no one among the people except her. One day she came to him and said: "My brother has a dispute with so-and-so, and I would love for you to judge in his favour when he comes to you."

He said: "Yes," but he did not do it. He was tested by his word, and he gave her his ring and entered the privy, and the devil came out in his form and said to her: "Give me the ring."

She gave it to him, and he came and sat in Sulayman's place. Sulayman came out after him and asked her to give him his ring.

She said: "Did you not take it before?"

He said: "No," and he went away from his place bewildered. The devil remained judging among the people for forty days.

He said: "The people denounced his judgement. The reciters and scholars of the Children of Israel gathered and came to his wives and said: 'We have denounced this. If this is Sulayman, then his mind has gone, and we denounce his judgements.' The women then wept." He said: "They came walking until they reached him, surrounded him, then opened the Torah and read it. When they read the Torah, it flew from between their hands until it alighted on a battlement, with the ring along with it. Then it flew until it went to the sea, and the ring fell from it into the sea, and a whale swallowed it."

He said: "Sulayman went on in the state he was in, until he came to a fisherman from the fishermen of the sea. He was hungry and his hunger had grown severe, so he asked him for some of their catch and said: 'I am Sulayman.'"

One of them rose to him and struck him with a stick, splitting his head.

He said: "He began washing his blood while on the shore of the sea. The fishermen blamed their companion who had struck him and said: 'What an evil thing you did in striking him.'"

He said: "He said: 'He claims he is Sulayman.' They gave him two fish from among what had already begun to spoil with them. The pain of his beating did not distract him, until he went to the edge of the sea, split open their bellies and began washing them, and found his ring in the belly of one of them. He took it and put it on, and Allah restored to him his kingdom and splendour, and the birds came and hovered over him, so the people knew that he was Sulayman, and they rose making excuses for what they had done."

He said: "I do not praise you for your excuse, nor do I blame you for what happened from you; this was a matter that had to be."

Then he came until he reached his kingdom, and commanded that the devil who had taken his ring be brought. He put him in an iron chest, sealed it, closed it with a lock, stamped it with his ring, and then commanded that it be cast into the sea, where he remains alive until the Hour." [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/38; Tarikh al-Tabari 1/354.]

In some reports: when Sulayman was tried, the ring fell from his hand, and his kingdom was in it. Sulayman took it and returned it to his hand, but it fell from his hand again. When Sulayman saw that it would not stay on his hand, he was certain of the trial, and Asaf said to Sulayman: "You are tried for your sin, and the ring will not hold fast on your hand for fourteen days. Flee to Allah repentant of your sin, and I will stand in your place, go about in your world and your households with your conduct, until Allah accepts your repentance and returns you to your kingdom."

So Sulayman fled, running to his Lord, and Asaf took the ring and placed it on his hand, and it held. And the body of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾ was Asaf, who was a scribe for Sulayman and had knowledge of the Book. Asaf remained in Sulayman's kingdom and world, going about by his conduct and acting by his deeds for fourteen days, until Sulayman returned to his dwelling repentant to Allah the Exalted, and Allah restored his kingdom to him. Asaf then rose from his seat, Sulayman sat on his throne, and he put the ring back on his hand, and it held there.

Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar informed us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that Sulayman ibn Dawud secluded himself from the people for three days, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "O Sulayman, you secluded yourself from the people for three days, and so you did not look into the affairs of My servants, and did not give justice to the oppressed against the oppressor."

He mentioned the hadith of the ring and the devil's seizing it as we have narrated it [in full in Tarikh Dimashq 22/248, ed. Dar al-Fikr].

At its end he said: "'Ali said: I mentioned that to al-Hasan, and he said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not have given him power over his wives.'" [al-Durr al-Manthur 5/312.]

Some exegetes said: The cause of Solomon's trial was that he had been commanded not to marry any woman except from the Children of Israel, but he married a woman from outside them, and he was punished for that.

It is also said: When Solomon took the daughter of the king of Sidon, he was impressed by her, so he invited her to Islam. She refused and resisted, so Solomon threatened her.

She said: "If you force me to embrace Islam, I will kill myself."

Solomon feared she would kill herself, so he married her while she was still a polytheist. For forty days she worshipped an idol of hers made of ruby, secretly from Solomon, until she embraced Islam. Solomon was punished by the loss of his kingdom for forty days.

Al-Sha'bi said regarding the cause: A son was born to Solomon. The devils gathered, and some of them said to others: "If he lives and has a child, we will not be freed from what we are in of affliction and of sorcery. Our way is to kill his child or to harm him."

Solomon learned of this, so he commanded the clouds, and the wind carried his son in the clouds, lest the devil harm him. Allah punished him for his fear of the devil, and the child died. He was cast dead onto his throne, and this is the body that Allah, glorified is He, mentioned: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back (in repentance).﴾ (38:34)

It is also said: Solomon said one day: "Tonight I will go around to all my wives, so that from each one of them a son will be born who will fight in the way of Allah." He did not say "if Allah wills" (in sha' Allah), so he had intercourse with all of them in one night, and none of them bore anything except a half-formed child. The midwife brought it and placed it on Solomon's throne.

This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿a body﴾. This is what was narrated to us by Abdullah ibn Hamid from others, who said: Ibn al-Sharqi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Aqil and Ahmad ibn Hafs narrated to us, both saying: Hafs narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to me from Musa ibn 'Uqba, who said: Abu al-Zinad informed me from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sulayman ibn Dawud said: 'Tonight I will go around to seventy women, each of whom will bring forth a horseman who will fight in the way of Allah.' His companion said to him: 'Say: if Allah wills.' But he did not say: 'if Allah wills.' So he went around to them, and none of them conceived except one woman, who brought forth half a man. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if he had said: 'if Allah wills,' they would all have fought in the way of Allah as horsemen." [116] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/209; Sahih Muslim: 5/87.]]

This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
﴿And We indeed tested Solomon.﴾

Muqatil said: Solomon was tested after he had ruled for twenty years, and he ruled for twenty years after the trial.

﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾, that is, a devil, according to most exegetes.

They differed about his name. Muqatil and Qatada said: His name is Sakhr ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amr ibn Sharahil, and he is the one who showed Solomon the diamond (al-almas) when he commanded that the Temple of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) be built, and it was said to him: "Let no sound of iron be heard in it." So they took the diamond and began to cut the stones and the jewels with it, and no sound was heard. Whenever Solomon wished to enter the privy (al-khala') or the bath, he would not enter with his ring. He entered the bath, and the story is mentioned about the devil's taking of the ring.

He said: Among them there was a man whom they compared with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab in strength. He said: "By Allah, I will test him." So he said: "O Prophet of Allah," while he did not see that he was the Prophet of Allah: "Do you see that if one of us becomes impure from sexual intercourse on a cold night, and he deliberately leaves washing until the sun rises, is there any harm upon him?" He said: "No." So he granted him leave in that, and he mentioned the hadith.

Abu Ishaq narrated from 'Imara ibn 'Abd from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "While Solomon was sitting on the shore of the sea playing with his ring, it fell into the sea, and his kingdom was in his ring."

Hammad ibn Salama narrated from 'Amr ibn Dinar from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The engraving on the ring of Sulayman ibn Dawud was: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." [117] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/498, no. 32337; Tadhkirat al-Mawdu'at: 108.]]

Returning to the hadith of 'Ali, he said: Solomon departed and left a devil in his household, and he came to an old woman and took refuge with her. The old woman said to him: "If you wish to go and seek (work), I will take care of the household work for you; or if you wish, you take care of the house and go and search."

He said: So he went searching. He came upon some people fishing, and he sat with them. They threw him some fish, so he took them and went to the old woman. She began to prepare them, and she split open the belly of a fish, and in it was the ring. She took it and said to Solomon: "What is this?"

Solomon took it and put it on, and the devils, the jinn, humans, birds, and beasts came to him. The devil who had been left in his household fled, and he came to an island in the sea. They sent devils to him, and they said: "We cannot overcome him, but he comes to us on the island once every seven days, one day. We cannot overcome him until he becomes intoxicated."

He said: So they drained its water and put wine in it. He said: When the day of his arrival came, he found the wine, and he said: "By Allah, you are indeed a good drink, except that you affect the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance." Then he left, until he became very thirsty, and then he came to it and said: "Indeed you are a good drink, except that you affect the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance."

He said: Then he drank it until it overcame his mind. Then they showed him the ring, and he said: "I hear and obey." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 22/187.]]

He said: So they brought him to Solomon, who bound him and then sent him to a mountain. It is said that it is the mountain of smoke that they see from him, and the water that comes out of the mountain is his urine.

Al-Suddi said: The name of that devil is Ismadhi, and it was said Khabfiq.

Mujahid said: His name is Asif.

Abu Salih ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Bayhaqi, the jurist, informed us, saying: Abu Hatim al-Tamimi informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar al-'Abdi narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubada narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us from Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid regarding ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾, who said: "A devil called Asif." Solomon said to him: "How do you deceive the people?"

He said: "Show me your ring, and I will tell you." When he gave it to him, he threw it into the sea. Solomon wandered, and his kingdom was lost. Asif sat on his throne, and Allah prevented Solomon's wives from him, so he did not approach them. The people denied Solomon's affair. Solomon used to ask for food and say: "Do you recognize me? I am Solomon," but they would deny him, until one day a woman gave him a fish. He split its belly and found his ring in its belly. His kingdom returned to him, and Asif fled and entered the sea. It was also said: The body is Asif ibn Barkhiya, the truthful, and the story has passed.

It is also said: It is the dead child who was carried off in the clouds.

It is also said: It is the child with a deformed creation.

It is also said: The meaning of His words ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾ is that Solomon was struck by an illness from which he approached death, until he became a body in the proverbial sense, without a soul. The emaciated sick person is described with this description, and it is said: "Like a body cast down," and nothing remained of him except his body. The sense of the verse is: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾.

As for the description of Solomon's throne:
It is narrated that when Solomon became king after his father, he commanded that a throne be made for him to sit on for judgment, and he commanded that it be made wondrous and awe-inspiring, such that if a wrongdoer or a false witness saw it, he would be restrained and awed.

He said: So there was made for him a throne of elephant tusks, inlaid with rubies, pearls, chrysolite, and various kinds of jewels, and surrounded by four palm trees of gold, whose clusters were of red ruby and green emerald. On the top of two of the palm trees were two golden peacocks, and on the top of the other two were two golden eagles, facing one another. On both sides of the throne were two golden lions, on the top of each of which was a pillar of green emerald. Vines of red gold were woven over the palm trees, and their clusters were of red ruby, such that the arbor of vines shaded the palm trees and the throne.

He said: When Solomon wished to ascend it, he placed his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne turned with what was on it, like a swiftly spinning millstone. The eagles and peacocks spread their wings, and the two lions stretched out their paws and struck the ground with their tails. This was done at every step that Solomon ascended. When he settled at the top, the two eagles on the palm trees took Solomon's crown and placed it on his head. Then the throne turned with what was on it, and the eagles, peacocks, and lions turned with it, their heads inclined toward Solomon, and they sprinkled upon him musk and ambergris from their bellies. Then a golden dove standing on a pillar of jewel, one of the pillars of the throne, took the Torah, and Solomon opened it and read it to the people and called them to a decisive judgment. The nobles of the Children of Israel sat on golden inlaid chairs—there were a thousand chairs—on his right, and the great ones of the jinn came and sat on silver chairs on his left—there were a thousand chairs—all surrounding him. Then the birds encircled them, shading them. The people came forward to him for judgment. When the clear proofs were called for and the witnesses came forward to give testimony, the throne turned with all that was around it, like a swiftly spinning millstone. The two lions stretched out their paws and struck the ground with their tails, and the two eagles and two peacocks spread their wings. The witnesses were terrified by it, and great fear entered them, so they bore witness only to the truth. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/202.]]

﴿He said: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾ (38:35)

Ibn Kaysan said: That is, it will not belong to anyone.

﴿after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾ — "al-Wahhab" means the Giver.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: He means: "Grant me a kingdom that I will not be stripped of for the rest of my life, as I was stripped of it in the past of my life."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Solomon was a king, but by his words ﴿that will not befit anyone after me﴾ he meant the subjugation of the winds and the birds, as indicated by what follows it.

It is also said: He asked for that so that it would be a sign of his prophethood, a proof of his messengership, and a miracle for those other than him.

It is also said: He asked for that so that it would be a sign to him of forgiveness and the acceptance of repentance, since Allah, glorified and exalted, answered his supplication, returned his kingdom to him, and increased it.

'Umar ibn 'Uthman al-Sadafi said: He meant by it the dominion over the self and the subjugation of desire.

This is supported by what:
'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Ifriqi narrated to us, saying: Salman ibn 'Amir al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Have you seen Solomon and what Allah gave him of kingship? He never raised his gaze to the sky in humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until Allah took him." [118] [[Al-Musannaf li Ibn Abi Shayba: 8/118.]]

And Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us, saying: Abu al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubada narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us from al-Hasan that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A devil appeared to me last night in my prayer place, like this dog of yours. I seized him and wanted to tie him up until morning, but I remembered the supplication of my brother Solomon: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me,﴾ so I let him go." [119] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/313.]]

And from him, from Rawh, from Shu'ba, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Last night a powerful jinn kept coming at me to cut off my prayer, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, enabled me to overcome him. [In the manuscript: 'fa-rra'ahu'; in the sources: 'fa-akhadhtahu,' 'fa-dha'tahu,' and 'fa-intahartuhu.'] I almost wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque until morning, so that you would all look at him. Then I remembered the words of Solomon: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me,﴾ so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him back defeated." [120] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/298; Sahih al-Bukhari: 4/136.]]

﴿So We subjected to him the wind, flowing gently by his command, wherever he willed.﴾ (38:36)

"Rukhaa'" means gentle and soft. "Haythu asaba" means wherever he intended and willed, in the language of Himyar.

The Arabs say: "asaba al-sawab wa akhta'a al-jawab," meaning he intended the correct answer.

The poet said:
"He hit upon the speech but could not (sustain it),
so he erred in the answer at the critical point." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/205; Tafsir al-Tha'alibi: 5/69.]]
