﴿And the devils﴾, that is, We subjected to him the devils: ﴿every builder and diver﴾, who extract pearls for him from the sea. He was the first to extract pearls from the sea. ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, meaning bound in chains—its singular is "sifd." ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold, without account.﴾ (38:39)

"Fa-mnun" means: give, from the words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿and do not give (favor) seeking to gain more﴾ (74:6).

The Arabs say: "manna 'alayya bi-raghif," meaning he gave me a loaf of bread.

Al-Hasan said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has never given anyone a gift without making an accounting in it, except Solomon, for Allah, glorified is He, gave him a pleasant gift, and he said: ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow﴾.

﴿or withhold, without account﴾ — he said: if he gives, he will be rewarded, and if he does not give, there will be no blame upon him.

Muqatil said: It concerns the matter of the devils: take whomever you wish of them into your bonds; there is no blame upon you for what you undertake.

﴿Indeed, for him with Us is a near station and a good final return.﴾ (38:40)

"Zulfa" means nearness, and "husn ma'ab" means a good place of return.

﴿And remember Our servant Job.﴾ (38:41)

Muqatil said: His kunya was Abu 'Abd Allah.

﴿When he called to his Lord: "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."﴾ (38:41) — that is, with fatigue, difficulty, affliction, and harm.

Muqatil said: "Hardship" refers to the body, and "torment" refers to his wealth.

There are four readings of "nusb": "nusub" with two dammas, which is the reading of Abu Ja'far; "nasab" with a fatha on the nun and the sad, which is the reading of Ya'qub; "nasb" with a fatha on the nun and a sukun on the sad, which is the transmission of Hubayra from Hafs from 'Asim; and "nasb" with a damma on the nun and a sukun on the sad, which is the reading of the rest.

They differed about the cause of Job's trial:
Wahb said: A man sought Job's help against an injustice he wanted to ward off, but he did not help him, and so he was tested.

Hayyan narrated from al-Kalbi that Job used to fight a king who was an unbeliever, and Job's livestock were in that king's territory. He flattered the king and did not fight him, so he was tested.

Others said: Job had abundant wealth, and he was impressed by his wealth, so he was tested.

﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and drink.﴾ (38:42) — "irkud" means push and move, and "hadha mughtasal" means this is a place to wash.

Then We sent forth for him another cool spring, and he said: "This is cool and a drink."

﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.﴾ (38:43)

﴿And take in your hand a bundle of grass (dighth), and strike with it and do not break your oath.﴾ (38:44) — "dighth" means a bundle of grass.

﴿Indeed, We found him patient. An excellent servant; indeed, he was one who turned back (to Allah) often.﴾ (38:44)

And remember Our servants.

The general readers recite it with the alif (ʿibādanā).

Ibn Kathir recited "ʿabdanā" in the singular, and this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbas.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf the jurist informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Bilal informed us, saying: Yahya ibn al-Rabi al-Makki narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn ʿAta, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he used to recite: "And remember Our servant Ibrahim." And he would say: "Indeed [Allah] mentioned Ibrahim and then his offspring after him: ﴿and Ishaq and Yaʿqub, people of strength and vision﴾ — strength in worship, and vision (al-absar) meaning insight into knowledge and religion — ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Abode﴾."

The people of Madina recited it with the genitive (idafa, "ʿabdi"), and this is the transmission of Hisham from the Syrians.

The others recited it with tanwin, in apposition (badal): ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen, the best﴾. ﴿And remember Ismaʿil, al-Yasaʿ and Dhu al-Kifl, and each is among the best. This is a remembrance.﴾ ﴿And indeed for the God-fearing is a good place of return: Gardens of Eden, their doors opened for them, reclining therein, calling therein for abundant fruit and drink. And with them will be women restraining their gaze, of equal age.﴾ Meaning: women of equal station, daughters of one woman, thirty-three years old. Its singular is "tarb" (peer). ﴿This is what you are promised﴾, with the taa (tu'aduna).

Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr and the rest recited it with the yaa (yuʿadu).

﴿for the Day of Reckoning﴾, meaning: on the day of reckoning.

Al-Aʿsha said:

"The humiliated, what is wrong with them in an evil time... until, when it recovers, they recover."

Meaning: in an evil time.

﴿Indeed this is Our provision, which has no end﴾, meaning: no destruction or extinction.

﴿This. And indeed for the transgressors, the evil place of return: Hell, they will burn therein, so wretched is the resting place.﴾ "This" refers to: this punishment. ﴿So let them taste it: boiling water and ghassaq.﴾

Al-Farra said: "I have put 'ḥamīm' and 'ghassāq' in the nominative governed by 'hadhā' (this), placed first and last; the meaning is: this is boiling water and ghassaq, so let them taste it. And if you wish, you may take it as a new sentence, complete in itself, and say: 'This, so let them taste it,' then say: 'of it is boiling water and ghassaq.'"

As in the words of the poet:

"Until, when the dawn lit up in the darkness, and the herbage was left, twisted and mown."

The readers differed over ﴿ghassāq﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf and Hafs read it with shaddah, and this is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdullah. The others read it without shaddah.

Al-Farra said: "Whoever reads it with shaddah makes it a noun of the pattern fa''āl, like al-khabbāz (baker) and al-ṭabbākh (cook). Whoever reads it without shaddah makes it a noun of the pattern fiʿāl, like al-ʿadhāb (punishment)."

The exegetes differed about it:

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the zamharir (extreme cold), which burns them with its cold as the fire burns them.

Mujahid and Muqatil said: it is the cold ice whose cold has reached its extreme; that is, it is the "mubīn" in the language of the Tahariyya, and "the provision" has reached it.

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: it is the essence/pus of the people of the Fire.

Qatada and al-Akhfash said: it is what flows from the sores of the disbelievers and fornicators between their flesh and skins, that is, what runs out.

A poet said:

"When I remember life and its pleasures, and tears flowed from my eye, flowing."

"And other [punishments]": the people of Basra and Mujahid read "wa-ukharu" with a damma on the alif, as the plural of "ukhrā"; Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim preferred it, because it describes it with a plural, saying: "arwah mithl al-kubra wa al-kubar" (of the same kind as the greater and greater).

The others read it in the singular: "wa-ākharu."

﴿of its kind﴾, meaning: like it. ﴿pairs﴾: kinds of punishment. The pronoun in "shaklihi" refers back to the punishment mentioned in "hādhā."

As for His saying ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is that when the leaders (qada) enter the Fire, and the followers (atbaʿ) enter after them, the guardians (khazana) say to the leaders: "This", meaning the followers, ﴿a troop﴾, a group, ﴿rushing in with you﴾ into the Fire, meaning: entering it as you entered.

The leaders say: ﴿No welcome for them﴾, meaning for the followers. ﴿Indeed they will burn in the Fire﴾, as we burned. The followers then say to the leaders: ﴿Rather, you: no welcome for you! You brought this upon us﴾, meaning: you established and set disbelief for us, ﴿so wretched is the abode﴾, meaning our abode and yours. "Al-marhab" and "al-rahb" mean spaciousness, and from it comes "rahbat al-masjid" (the open courtyard of the mosque).

Abu ʿUbayda said: the Arabs say to a man, "lā marḥaban bika," meaning, "May the earth not be wide for you," i.e., "may it not be spacious."

Al-Qutaybi said: the meaning of their saying "marḥaban, ahlan wa sahlan" is: you have come to a wide and spacious place, you have come to ease and not hardship, you have come to your own people and not as strangers; so be at ease and do not feel alienated. It is in the manner of supplication, as you say, "You have met good," and therefore it is put in the accusative.

The poet al-Nabigha said:

"No welcome to tomorrow, nor family with it, if the separation of loved ones is tomorrow."

﴿"You are averse to it."﴾ ﴿"I had no knowledge of the Highest Assembly when they disputed"﴾ — concerning the matter of Adam, namely their saying when Allah said to them: ﴿"Indeed, I am going to place a successive authority upon the earth."﴾ They said: ﴿"Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein?"﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 30.]] — this is the statement of most of the exegetes.

Ibn 'Abbas narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "My Lord said: 'Do you know what the Highest Assembly, meaning the angels, dispute about?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'They dispute about expiations and degrees. As for expiations: perfecting ablution in difficult conditions, walking to congregational prayers, and waiting for one prayer after another. As for degrees: spreading the greeting of peace, feeding people, and praying at night while people are asleep.'" [121] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/226.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 38, verse 71–88:

When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] spirit, fall down to him in prostration." So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely, except Iblis; he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers. [Allah] said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Are you arrogant, or have you been among the haughty?" He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay." [Allah] said, "Then get out of it, for indeed, you are expelled. And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense." He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the day they are resurrected." [Allah] said, "Indeed, you are of those reprieved until the day of the time well known." He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except among them Your chosen servants." [Allah] said, "So the truth [I say], and the truth I speak."

And in the verification of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, the formation with the hand is evidence that it does not mean blessing, power, or capability; rather, these are two attributes of His Essence.

Mujahid said: "The hand here means emphasis, and the connection is metaphorical: 'what I created' (lima khalaqtu), like His statement, glorified is He: 'And there remains the Face of your Lord' [Surah al-Rahman: 27], meaning your Lord." This interpretation is not strong, because if it meant mere connection, Iblis could have said: "If You created him, You have also created me." Likewise regarding power and blessing: Adam would have no distinction over Iblis in creation. This matter has already been discussed at His statement: "Of what Our hands have made" [Surah Ya-Sin: 71].

He said: The Arabs use the dual to refer to both, as in His statement, glorified is He: "These are two adversaries who dispute" [Surah al-Hajj: 19], and His statement: "And let a group of the believers witness their punishment" [Surah al-Nur: 2]. He said: "They are two men." And He said: "Your hearts have certainly inclined" [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].

"Aistakbarta" — the interrogative alif enters upon the alif of information: "Am I among the exalted?" meaning, among those who are arrogant toward prostrating, like His statement, glorified is He: "Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land" [Surah al-Qasas: 4]. Iblis said: "I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay." [Allah] said: "Then get out of it," meaning: out of Paradise.

It is said: out of the heavens.

Al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Out of the form of creation in which you are."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "This is the correct interpretation, because Iblis acted tyrannically and boasted about his creation, so Allah, exalted is He, altered his form: he became black after having been white, ugly after having been beautiful, and dark after having been luminous."

"For indeed, you are accursed" — expelled and tormented. "And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense." He said: "My Lord, then reprieve me until the day they are resurrected." [Allah] said: "Indeed, you are of those reprieved until the day of the time well known," which is the first blast. He said: "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except among them Your chosen servants." [Allah] said: "So the truth [I say], and the truth I speak."

Mujahid, al-A'mash, 'Asim, Hamzah and Khalaf recited: with the first in the nominative and the second in the accusative, with the meaning "So I am the truth," or "So from Me is the truth, and I say the truth."

The rest recited both in the accusative.

The grammarians differed regarding their two readings. It was said: the first is in the accusative as an incitement (al-igra'), and the second by the verb of saying governing it.

It was said: the first is an oath, and the second is an object: "By the truth," which is Allah, mighty and majestic, swore by Himself: "and the truth I speak."

It was said: He followed one oath with another.

Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayd said: their meaning is "verify," without the definite article, as one says "al-hamdu lillah" and "ahmadu Allah"; both have the same meaning.

Talhah ibn Musarrif recited: "fa-l-haqqu wa-l-haqqi" with the genitive, so both are an oath.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdash say: it is referred back to what precedes it, and its implied meaning is: "By Your might, and by the truth, and the truth," Allah said: "I will surely fill Hell with you," i.e., with you and your offspring, "and with whoever follows you of them all." "Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it," i.e., for conveying the revelation, a pronoun referring to something unmentioned, "any wage." Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this verse abrogates His statement: "Say: I do not ask you for it any reward, except affection among relatives" [Surah al-Shura: 23].

"And I am not of those who presume" — those who fabricate the Qur'an from their own selves.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Banusti Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Umayr ibn Yusuf told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Awf told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, saying: Hanwah ibn Suraij ibn Yazid told us, saying: Arta'ah ibn al-Mundhir told us, from Damrah ibn Habib, from Salamah ibn Muqbil, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The presumptuous one has three signs: he contends with one above him, he reaches for what is not attainable, and he speaks about what he does not know." [122] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/231.]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: al-Sunni told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far told me, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi told us, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Sayf ibn 'Umar al-Dabbi told us, from Wa'il ibn Dawud, from Yazid al-Bahi, from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, who said: The herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "O Allah, forgive those who invoke the dead of my community and do not presume, except that I am free of presumption; and reconcile my community." [123] [See: Tadhkirat al-Mawdu'at: 67.]

And al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ibn Shaybah told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Amr ibn Bakr al-Sakasiki at Bayt al-Maqdis told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn [........] [illegible text] 'Allyah al-Zuhri told us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "O people, whoever Allah, mighty and majestic, has given knowledge, let him fear Allah and teach it to the people and not conceal it, for whoever conceals knowledge he knows is like one who conceals what Allah sent down to His Prophet and commanded him to teach the people. Whoever does not know, let him be silent; and beware of saying what he does not know, lest he perish, become one of the presumptuous, and pass out of the religion. Indeed, Allah, mighty and majestic, said: 'Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it, and I am not of those who presume.'" Whoever gives a fatwa without the Sunnah, upon him is the sin.

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: al-Sunni told us, saying: Abu Khalifah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khabir al-'Abdi told us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "O people, whoever knows something, let him speak of it; and whoever does not know something, let him say: 'Allah knows best,' for part of knowledge is that one says of what he does not know, 'Allah knows best.' Indeed, Allah, mighty and majestic, said to His Prophet: 'Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it, and I am not of those who presume. It is not but a reminder to the worlds, and you will surely know its news after a time.'"

Qatadah said: it means after death.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the Day of Resurrection.
